compliment: Cook's in a flap over the Duke's cake. Go and help him, traveller.
insult: Cook's still short of an egg. Any chance? No? Thought not.
plain/insult: The Cook needs an egg. It's an egg. Chickens manage it daily.
remark: Cook's been in that kitchen panicking all week.
starter/compliment: Oh! You look a helpful sort. Could you fetch me an egg?
Please, adventurer, I'm desperate. Eggs, milk, flour!
starter/insult: Oh dear, oh dear. You wouldn't carry flour, would you? Nobody does.
starter/remark: Eggs... milk... flour... the Duke's cake... I'm done for.
Four children and a goat, and now no flour.

compliment: Word is you saved the Duke's birthday cake. Lovely.
The Cook's actually smiling. Your doing, they say.
insult: I hear you fetched an egg for the Cook. The bards are still deciding.
remark: The town crier was going on about some cake. Was that you?
starter/compliment: Oh, hello again! That cake went down a treat, you know.
starter/insult: Wipe your feet, egg-fetcher. I've just mopped.
Oh. You again. Still dining out on that cake, are you?
starter/remark: The Duke wants another cake. Don't look at me like that.
rough/insult: Fetched an egg for the castle, did ye? Blimey. A hero.
barkeep/insult: Saved a cake, I hear. In my kitchen we call that a morning.
kid/insult: You got the Cook an egg. I get eggs every day. Where's my cake?

compliment: The Duke's found a curious talisman. He's after someone clever.
insult: The Duke's talisman still needs taking to the wizards. It's not far.
remark: Funny goings-on with talismans at the castle, I hear.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer! I've found the most curious talisman.
starter/insult: You there. You'll do. Take this talisman somewhere useful.
starter/remark: Hmm. What on earth is this talisman for? Most peculiar.

compliment: I hear you're the one who found out how runes are made. Clever.
Word at the Wizards' Tower is you cracked that talisman.
insult: I hear you carried a parcel to a wizard. Any chance you'd carry mine?
remark: Aubury's been ever so busy since you came along, I hear.
starter/compliment: My dear adventurer! Still making runes, I trust?
starter/insult: Ah. The parcel courier. Do come in. Or don't.
starter/remark: The wizards still write to me about you, you know.

compliment: Father Aereck's got a ghost in his graveyard. Pop over, would you?
insult: A ghost in the churchyard, and you've walked past it twice now.
remark: They say there's a ghost in that graveyard. Gives me the shivers.
starter/compliment: Greetings, traveller! A moment? A spirit troubles my graveyard.
starter/insult: Ah, a visitor. You wouldn't fancy a word with a ghost, would you? No.
starter/remark: Saradomin give me strength. That ghost was moaning all night again.

compliment: Word is you laid Lumbridge's ghost to rest. Lovely thing.
insult: I hear you gave a ghost its skull back. It only took a few centuries.
remark: My gran says the graveyard's gone quiet. That you, was it?
starter/compliment: Ah, my friend! The graveyard's been at peace since you helped.
starter/insult: Thank you again for the ghost. Sorry, I only had the one quest.
starter/remark: Not a peep from that ghost. I almost miss him.
kid/remark: You talked to a ghost? Was it see-through? What did it want?

compliment: Fred the Farmer needs his sheep shearing. Honest work, that.
insult: Fred's sheep are still waiting. They're more patient than Fred.
remark: Them sheep up Fred's farm are getting right woolly.
starter/compliment: You there! Fancy shearing my sheep for a few coins?
starter/insult: You look like you've never held shears. Prove me wrong.
starter/remark: Twenty balls of wool. Where am I going to find twenty?
That sheep's looking at me again.
rough/remark: Fred's sheep want shearing. He'll not do it himself, mind.

compliment: I hear you sheared every sheep on Fred's farm. Champion.
insult: Word is you sheared some sheep. The sheep tell it differently.
remark: Fred's sheep look positively chilly since you came by.
starter/compliment: Ah, it's my favourite shearer! How you keeping?
starter/insult: Oi, shearer. That sheep's still not forgiven you, you know.
starter/remark: Sheep are getting woolly again. No pressure.
rough/compliment: Sheared Fred's whole flock, I hear. Ye can do mine next.

compliment: Veos at the pub's after a treasure hunter. Right up your street.
insult: Veos's treasure is still buried. It's a spade and a map, traveller.
remark: Bloke in the Sheared Ram keeps on about buried treasure.
starter/compliment: Fancy yourself a treasure hunter? I've a map that needs reading.
starter/insult: You look like you'd lose a spade in a bucket. Still, come on.
starter/remark: Where's that treasure... the scroll says it's round here somewhere.
barkeep/remark: Veos has nursed one drink all week, going on about treasure.

compliment: I hear you found Veos's treasure. Good on you.
insult: Word is you dug holes all over Lumbridge. Fill them in, would you?
starter/compliment: My favourite digger! Fancy another adventure?
starter/insult: Ah, my little digging assistant. Back for more holes?
barkeep/insult: Dug up Lumbridge for Veos, I hear. He still owes for his ale.

compliment: Adventurers by the swamp are after a lost city. Zanaris, they say.
Those adventurers won't say what they're after. The warrior might.
insult: Those adventurers have been at the swamp for weeks. Zanaris, indeed.
plain/insult: Camped in a swamp for weeks and found nothing. You'd fit right in.
remark: The leprechaun in the swamp knows a thing or two, I hear.
gossip: That lot by the swamp are after Zanaris, the warrior let slip. Loudly.
A leprechaun hides in one of those trees, they say. Not saying which.
starter/compliment: Hello there, traveller! We're not here for any reason at all. None.
starter/insult: Adventurers of our calibre don't hang about in forests for fun, whelp!
starter/remark: We're looking for Zanaris... Gah! I mean we're not. Forget I spoke.

compliment: Word is you found Zanaris. Dramen staff and everything!
insult: I hear you found a whole city. In a shed.
plain/insult: Found a magic city by walking into a shed. Try the privy next.
remark: That leprechaun's been telling everyone about you.
gossip: The archer by the swamp still can't believe who found that portal.
It was the shed all along, they say. The shed in the swamp.
starter/compliment: You found it? Well... good for you. Don't tell the others I helped.
starter/insult: A whelp like you found Zanaris? ...We're still not looking for it.
starter/remark: Still searching for Zanaris... Gah! We're not doing anything. Nope.

compliment: Romeo's pining for Juliet again. Help the poor lad out?
insult: Romeo's still sighing in the square. Go on, you've nothing better on.
remark: Young love. Loud, isn't it?
starter/compliment: Excuse me! Have you seen my Juliet? Fairest maiden in Varrock!
starter/insult: You! You look clever. Where do people keep Juliets?
starter/remark: Oh, Juliet... wherefore art thou... no, really, where are you?
barkeep/remark: Romeo's been in here sighing into his drink. Lost a Juliet.
guard/remark: Moved Romeo along twice today. He'll be back. Sighing.

compliment: I hear you helped Romeo and Juliet. Ever so romantic.
insult: Played matchmaker for two youngsters, I hear. Did anyone ask Dad?
remark: Romeo's been going round telling everyone about you.
starter/compliment: My friend! You helped me and Juliet! Well, sort of. Thanks!
starter/insult: Oh, it's you. The reason Juliet doesn't write any more.
starter/remark: Juliet? Who's Juliet? Oh, her. Yes. Lovely.
guard/remark: Quiet in the square since you sorted Romeo out. Too quiet.

compliment: Aris says a demon's coming for Varrock. You look the type.
insult: A demon's due south of the walls. Don't let it spoil your shopping.
remark: The fortune teller's ever so worried about a demon.
starter/compliment: Cross my palm with silver, dear. I see a great destiny!
starter/insult: The ball shows a hero. Then it shows you. Odd, that.
starter/remark: Delrith... Delrith... the ball keeps showing me that demon.
kid/remark: A demon's coming and Mum says I can't watch.
guard/remark: Fortune teller says a demon's coming. Not on my shift, it isn't.
guard/gossip: Word from the palace: nothing about a demon. So there's no demon.

compliment: Word is you saw off Delrith. Varrock owes you one.
Varrock's still here. Aris says that's down to you.
insult: Killed a demon with Sir Prysin's sword, I hear. Does he know?
remark: Sir Prysin's been bragging about handing you Silverlight.
starter/compliment: Ah, my hero! The crystal ball still shows you, dear.
starter/insult: The crystal ball says you'll never top that demon, dear. Never.
barkeep/compliment: You're the one who saw off that demon? First one's on me, love.
kid/compliment: You stabbed a demon with a shiny sword? Show me the sword!
kid/insult: Sir Prysin gave you the sword. So he really killed it.
guard/compliment: You're the one who saw off that demon? Carry on, then. Carefully.
guard/remark: A demon at the gates, and nobody filed a report.

compliment: Reldo in the palace library's got a tale about a stolen shield.
insult: That old shield's still missing. There's a whole library on it.
remark: There's gangs in Varrock, they say. Phoenix and Black Arm.
starter/compliment: Psst. You look like you'd enjoy a mystery. A stolen shield, perhaps?
starter/insult: Shh! Oh, it's you. Read something for once. Start with the shield.
starter/remark: Hmm, the old shield... stolen by a gang... fascinating.
guard/remark: Phoenix Gang, Black Arm Gang. I know where they are. Nobody asks.

compliment: I hear you got that old shield back for the museum. Very good.
insult: Joined a gang for a shield, I hear. Your mother must be thrilled.
remark: Which gang did you go with, then? Don't tell me.
starter/compliment: Ah, a reader! I've written you into the history books, you know.
starter/insult: Shh. Oh, it's you. You still owe the library three books.
guard/insult: Joined a gang to get a shield back, I hear. I'll be watching you.

compliment: King Roald needs a temple checking on. Out east, by the Salve.
insult: Nobody's checked on that temple by the Salve. Not even the brave ones.
remark: Something nasty about that temple out east, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, a capable sort! I need someone to look in on a temple.
starter/insult: Yes, citizen? Good. You'll do. There's a temple needs checking.
starter/remark: Not a word from that temple on the Salve. Most troubling.
guard/gossip: Word from the palace: the Salve temple's gone quiet. Not our problem.

compliment: Word is you saved the priest at the Salve temple. Good work.
insult: Killed the temple's dog because a door asked you to, I hear.
remark: They say you can get into Morytania now. Rather you than me.
starter/compliment: Ah, we received word from Drezel. Very good work, citizen.
starter/insult: A dog? In a temple? Are you a complete imbecile, citizen?
guard/remark: Back from the Salve, are you? Wipe your boots. Morytania mud.

compliment: Morgan's after someone to see off a vampyre. Bring garlic.
insult: Count Draynor's still at large. Lovely neck you've got, by the way.
remark: Draynor folk keep losing sleep. And blood.
starter/compliment: Could it be? A bold adventurer! Please, a vampyre plagues Draynor!
starter/insult: You there! Hurry! We're running out of necks!
starter/remark: Another bite last night... someone has to stop that Count.

compliment: Word is you staked Count Draynor. Draynor sleeps easy now.
I hear you're the vampyre slayer from Draynor. Brave.
insult: I hear you staked a vampyre who'd only just woken up. Sporting.
remark: Draynor folk have been buying garlic in your honour.
starter/compliment: My saviour! I sleep with the window open now, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Took you long enough. My cousin got bitten twice.
kid/compliment: You staked a vampyre? Did it go dusty? Did it scream?
kid/insult: Garlic. You beat a vampyre with garlic. I eat garlic.

compliment: Poor Veronica's fella went into that manor and never came out.
insult: Veronica's Ernest is still in that manor. Scared of the professor?
remark: The professor in that manor's a bit touched, they say.
starter/compliment: Oh, please, you look kind! My Ernest went into that manor!
starter/insult: Are you going to help me, or just stand there gawping?
starter/remark: Ernest... he said he'd only be a minute. That was hours ago.

compliment: I hear you turned Ernest back from a chicken. Well, mostly.
insult: Word is you un-chickened a man. They'll sing songs. Short ones.
remark: Ernest still pecks at his dinner, I hear.
starter/compliment: There you are! Ernest's ever so grateful. Nearly back to normal.
starter/insult: Ernest still clucks in his sleep, you know. Thanks for that.
kid/compliment: You turned a chicken back into a man? Do it to our rooster!

compliment: Hassan says Prince Ali's been kidnapped. Fancy a rescue?
insult: Prince Ali's still locked up. Heroes are thin on the ground, it seems.
remark: Al Kharid's in a right state about that prince.
starter/compliment: Friend! You look resourceful. Our prince has been taken!
starter/insult: You? Well. Beggars can't be choosers. The prince has been kidnapped.
starter/remark: The prince... gone. The Emir has not slept. Nor have I.

compliment: Word is you sprang Prince Ali from Lady Keli. Clever stuff.
insult: I hear you put a prince in a wig and a skirt. He suits it, mind.
remark: Lady Keli's still fuming about you, I hear.
starter/compliment: Ah, a friend of Al Kharid! The Emir speaks of you often.
starter/insult: The prince still won't take that skirt off. Your doing.

compliment: Wizard Mizgog's lost his beads to imps. Catch a few, would you?
insult: The imps still have Mizgog's beads. They're small imps, traveller.
remark: Imps everywhere round the tower. Little pests.
starter/compliment: Ah! You look quick on your feet. Fancy catching some imps?
starter/insult: Not now, I'm concentrating. Unless you're here about the imps?
starter/remark: Red bead... yellow bead... black, white... wretched imps.

compliment: I hear you got Mizgog's beads back off them imps. Lovely.
insult: Word is you spent a week chasing imps for some beads.
starter/compliment: Ah, the imp-catcher! My beads are still the shiniest in the tower.
starter/insult: My beads came back sticky. Imp sticky. Thanks ever so.

compliment: Hetty in Rimmington's brewing something. She needs a rat's tail.
insult: Hetty still needs a rat's tail. Rats aren't that frightening.
remark: Smells of eye of newt round Hetty's place.
starter/compliment: Ooh, dear. Fetch me a few bits and I'll teach you some magic.
starter/insult: You never know what shape you'll wake up in, dear. Rat's tail, please.
starter/remark: Eye of newt... burnt meat... onion... where's that rat's tail?

compliment: I hear you drank Hetty's potion. Brave, that.
insult: Word is you drank something out of a witch's cauldron. On purpose.
remark: Hetty's telling everyone how helpful you were. Suspicious.
starter/compliment: Ooh, hello again, dear! Come in for a brew?
starter/insult: Drank my potion in one go. Nobody does that, dear. Odd.

compliment: Doric needs clay, copper and iron. Honest work, that.
insult: Doric's still waiting on clay. It's clay. It just lies there.
remark: Doric's anvils are free to use, if you help him out.
starter/compliment: Hello, traveller! Fetch me some ores and you can use my anvils.
starter/insult: Hello, traveller. My grandmother mines faster. She's a rock.
starter/remark: Six clay, four copper, two iron... where's a helper when you need one.
dwarf/remark: Doric's waiting on ore. Clay, copper, iron. Nothing fancy.

compliment: Word is Doric lets you use his anvils. Proper trusted, you.
insult: Clay for Doric, I hear. Heavy work, if you count the walk.
starter/compliment: Ah, friend! The anvils are free for you, as always.
starter/insult: You brought me some clay. Shall I build you a statue? No.
rough/compliment: Doric lets ye at his anvils? He'll not let me near 'em.
dwarf/compliment: Doric lets you use his anvils? By Guthix, he doesn't let me.

compliment: The Squire's lost Sir Vyvin's sword. Help the lad out?
insult: The Squire's still sweating over that sword. You could at least look.
remark: Some daft squire's lost his master's sword, I hear.
starter/compliment: Oh, please! I've lost Sir Vyvin's sword and he'll have my head!
starter/insult: Unless you've a sword in your pocket, move along. Actually, wait!
starter/remark: Sir Vyvin will have my head... where did I put that sword?
rough/remark: Some squire's lost a sword. Lost! Ye don't lose a sword.
dwarf/remark: A lost sword and a nervous squire. Thurgo could sort it, for a pie.
guard/remark: Squire's lost Sir Vyvin's sword. Not my department.

compliment: I hear you saved that Squire's bacon. Very noble.
insult: Bribed a dwarf with pie for a sword, I hear. I'd have wanted two.
remark: Thurgo still asks after you. And his pie.
starter/compliment: Psst! Sir Vyvin never noticed a thing. I owe you!
starter/insult: Sir Vyvin keeps asking why his hilt's gone sparkly.
rough/remark: Blurite, they say. Off the ice. Rather ye than me.
dwarf/compliment: Thurgo forged you a blade? Imcando work. Treasure it.
guard/gossip: Sir Vyvin's sword turned up. Nobody's asking where. Good.

compliment: Sir Amik needs a spy in the Black Knights' Fortress. Hush-hush.
insult: The Black Knights are brewing something. Not that anyone's looked.
remark: The Black Knights are up to something, mark my words.
starter/compliment: You there! You look discreet. The White Knights need a spy.
starter/insult: Hmm. Not exactly the spy type. Still, you'll have to do.
starter/remark: What are those Black Knights brewing up there? It troubles me.
guard/gossip: Word from the castle: watch the north road. Black Knights about.

compliment: Word is you ruined the Black Knights' plans. Jolly good show.
insult: I hear you dropped a cabbage in a cauldron. A true warrior.
remark: Never look at a cabbage the same way now, do you?
starter/compliment: Ah, my spy! Splendid to see you again.
starter/insult: One cabbage. That was your grand contribution. Hmph.
guard/compliment: You're Sir Amik's spy? Didn't see you. Which is the point, I suppose.

compliment: The goblins are fighting over armour colours. Sort them out?
insult: Goblins still rowing over armour. Needs a diplomat. Or paint.
remark: Them goblins in Goblin Village are at it again.
gossip: Half the village in red, half in green, all shouting. Goblins.
The generals want new armour for the goblin new century, they say.
starter/compliment: Human! You look clever for human. Bring us armour in new colour!
starter/insult: Go away human, we busy. Unless you bring armour. You bring armour?
starter/remark: Not red. Red make you look fat. Not green. Green look naked. Hmph.

compliment: Word is you sorted out Wartface and Bentnoze. Proper diplomat.
insult: I hear you dyed some armour for goblins. Do they tip?
remark: Brown armour, wasn't it? Typical goblins.
gossip: Orange, then blue, then brown. Brown. They started with brown.
Grubfoot tried on every colour, they say. Looked like an orange-fruit.
starter/compliment: Human! Brown armour quite nice. Me can see myself wearing that.
starter/insult: Thank you for sorting argument, human. Now go. Human still ugly.
starter/remark: Brown armour it is. Was brown before. Shut up, Grubfoot.

compliment: Redbeard Frank's after some rum. Says he'll show you treasure.
insult: Redbeard's still dry. Nobody brave enough to fetch rum, it seems.
remark: That Redbeard Frank's always got a bottle on the go.
starter/compliment: Arr! Fetch me some Karamjan rum and I'll make it worth yer while.
starter/insult: Arr, ye look as useful as a chocolate cutlass. Fetch me rum anyway.
starter/remark: Arr... not a drop o' rum left... a pirate can't live like this.
pirate/remark: Frank's been dry a week. A dry pirate's a dangerous thing.
pirate/gossip: Redbeard says there's treasure for whoever fetches him rum. Says.
barkeep/remark: Frank's tab's longer than my arm, and he wants Karamja rum.

compliment: I hear you found old Redbeard's treasure. Lovely.
insult: Smuggled rum in with the bananas, I hear. The bananas never recovered.
remark: Somebody dug up Falador park. The gardener's still livid.
starter/compliment: Arr, hello again, me hearty! Ye be a pirate at heart.
starter/insult: Arr, ye ate half them bananas, didn't ye?
pirate/compliment: Ye got rum past the Customs men? Arr, ye're one of us now.
pirate/insult: Arr, all that for one casket. Old Hector buried his small.
rough/insult: Hid rum in the bananas, I hear. Wydin's still counting 'em.
barkeep/remark: Fetched Frank his rum, did you? Lovely. Now fetch me what he owes.
kid/insult: You dug up the park and only got one box? I'd have kept digging.
guard/insult: Somebody dug up the park. Wyson's filed a complaint. Several.

compliment: The Champions' Guild wants a dragon slain. You've the look for it.
insult: Elvarg's still alive. Mind, so are you. Coincidence, I'm sure.
remark: Elvarg's still out on Crandor, they say.
starter/compliment: Want to prove yourself? There's a dragon on Crandor needs seeing to.
starter/insult: A champion? You? Well. There's a dragon that might settle it.
starter/remark: Elvarg still lives... someone ought to do something about it.
kid/remark: There's a dragon on Crandor. Dad won't take me.

compliment: Word is you slew Elvarg. Proper champion, you.
You're the one who slew Elvarg? Blimey!
insult: Killed a dragon with a borrowed boat, I hear. Did Ned get it back?
remark: Ned's been telling everyone about that boat trip. Every day.
starter/compliment: Ah, a true hero! Welcome back, champion.
starter/insult: Killed one dragon. There's rather a lot more, you know.
kid/compliment: You killed a dragon? Did you keep its teeth? Can I have one?
kid/insult: Ned's boat got wrecked, Mum says. Did you break it?

compliment: The druids at Taverley will teach you herblore. See Kaqemeex.
insult: The druids are still waiting on their meat. Patient folk, druids.
remark: The druids at the stone circle are ever so friendly.
starter/compliment: Greetings, traveller. The druids could teach you the ways of herblore.
starter/insult: Hmm. Can you even tell a herb from a weed? Come, learn.
starter/remark: The ritual must be done... we need raw meats for the cauldron.

compliment: I hear you learnt herblore from the Taverley druids. Clever.
insult: Dipped meat in a cauldron, I hear. The druids call that a ritual.
starter/compliment: Greetings again, herbalist. Guthix smiles on you.
starter/insult: The druids still talk about your meat. Not kindly.

compliment: Almera's lad went down the river. Help her out, would you?
insult: Almera's lad's still down that river. Someone ought to look.
remark: Baxtorian's tomb's under them falls, they reckon.
starter/compliment: Oh, please, you look brave! My son Hudon went down the river!
starter/insult: Are you going to help, or just stand there admiring the waterfall?
starter/remark: Hudon... that silly boy and his treasure hunting...

compliment: Word is you found Baxtorian's chamber under the falls. Smashing.
insult: I hear you floated down a river on a log. Most folk use a boat.
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! Hudon's still sulking that you got there first.
starter/insult: Hudon says you stole his treasure. I say you can keep it.

compliment: King Bolren's gnomes need help against Khazard's troops.
insult: Bolren's still waiting. It's only a hedge maze, traveller.
remark: The gnomes in the maze are at war again.
starter/compliment: Welcome, human! You look strong. Our village needs help!
starter/insult: Ah, human. You made it through the maze. Eventually.
starter/remark: The orb is gone... the village is lost without it...
gnome/remark: Khazard's men at the village again. Bolren will be beside himself.

compliment: I hear you got the gnomes their orbs back. They love you.
insult: Lost in a hedge for an hour, I hear. Gnome children do it for fun.
remark: The spirit tree's lovely and green now, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, our human friend! The orbs are safe, thanks to you.
starter/insult: An hour in my maze. The children do it in ten minutes.
gnome/compliment: You brought the orbs back to Bolren? The spirit tree thanks you.
gnome/insult: Through the maze at last, human. We put signs up for you lot.

compliment: King Narnode's worried about the Grand Tree. Lend a hand?
insult: The Grand Tree's poorly. Not that sightseers notice.
remark: Something's eating at the Grand Tree's roots, they say.
starter/compliment: Welcome, traveller! Nice to see an outsider. The Grand Tree is sick!
starter/insult: Ah, human. Forgive me if I hope you're more use than the last one.
starter/remark: The Grand Tree's roots... something's eating them. But what?
gnome/remark: Narnode's been pacing round the Tree. Pacing's never good.

compliment: Word is you rumbled Glough. The gnomes owe you.
insult: I hear you found a rock under a tree. A parade is planned.
remark: Glough had it coming, if you ask me.
starter/compliment: Ah, human! The Grand Tree thrives, thanks to you.
starter/insult: You found a rock under my tree. I'd have got there eventually.
gnome/compliment: You're the human who caught Glough out? The Tree's green again.
gnome/insult: Glough, a traitor. And it took a human to notice. Hmph.

starter/compliment: Ah, human! I need an envoy. Would you look into the tenth squad?
starter/insult: Ape Atoll? Hmm. You'll have to do, I suppose.
starter/remark: The tenth squad... not a word from Ape Atoll. Worrying.
gossip: Narnode's after someone brave for Ape Atoll. Nobody's volunteered.
The monkeys on Ape Atoll are a rum lot.
The tenth squad went to Ape Atoll and never came back.

compliment: Word is you fought a jungle demon on Ape Atoll. Hard as nails.
You found the tenth squad on Ape Atoll? Alive? Blimey.
insult: Found the tenth squad, then left them on Ape Atoll. Thorough.
remark: Back from Ape Atoll smelling of bananas, I expect.
starter/compliment: Ah, my monkey-wrangling friend! You were magnificent.
starter/insult: Ah, human. Forgive me, but you still smell faintly of monkey.
gossip: The tenth squad are alive, so Narnode says. Still on Ape Atoll, mind.
kid/insult: You dressed up as a monkey? For a whole week?
plain/insult: Ape Atoll was perfectly quiet until you went poking about.
gnome/compliment: You found the tenth squad, human? Narnode hasn't stopped smiling.
gnome/insult: You still sit like a monkey, human. Habit, is it?

compliment: Brundt in Rellekka wants to see if you're Fremennik material.
insult: Still an outerlander? The Fremennik won't even sell you a fish.
remark: The Fremennik won't trade with outerlanders, you know.
starter/compliment: Greetings, outerlander! Prove yourself to the council and earn a name.
starter/insult: Hah! An outerlander. You'll never pass the trials. Try anyway.
starter/remark: Another outerlander. Will none of them prove worthy?
fremennik/remark: Our customs forbid me talking to you, outerlander. So I won't.
fremennik/insult: Seven of the twelve, outerlander. You'll be lucky to get one.
fremennik/gossip: Another outerlander trying for the council. They never last.

compliment: I hear the Fremennik gave you a name. Very rugged.
insult: Word is you drank a pint and played a lyre. A warrior's trials, those.
remark: What's your Fremennik name, then? Something silly, I bet.
starter/compliment: Well met, friend of the Fremennik! Welcome back.
starter/insult: Hah! Your Fremennik name still gets a laugh in the longhall.
fremennik/compliment: Hah! Well met. You drank Manni under the table, they say.
fremennik/insult: You beat Koschei, they say. Three times. Four would've impressed me.
fremennik/remark: A Fremennik name and a seat in the longhall. Don't waste either.

compliment: Word is you saved the whole Lumbridge banquet. Pudding and all.
I hear you saw off that mad chef. The council owes you dinner.
A cook from a hundred years back crashed a feast, and you saw him off.
They say you fed a king of monkeys his favourite dish. Takes nerve.
Dwarf, goblins, ogre, pirate and a knight. You cooked for the lot?
A demon made of bananas, they say. And you won. I need a sit-down.
insult: I hear it took you an age to save one dinner party.
Saved a feast, I hear. The washing-up was somebody else's problem?
All those dinners to cook before you could fight anyone. Patient sort.
remark: How's the Culinaromancer, eh? Not so cocky now.
An evil chicken's egg in a pudding, I'm told. Who thinks of that?
Duke Horacio's dinner saved by the help, they say. As usual.
pirate/compliment: Ye fed Pirate Pete a fishcake and he's still on about it. Arr.
barkeep/compliment: You saw off the Culinaromancer? Every cook in Gielinor owes you one.
dwarf/compliment: A rock cake off old Rohak, carried hot. By Guthix, that's dedication.
dwarf/remark: Rohak's rock cakes. You need gloves. Everyone learns that once.
kid/insult: You saved a whole dinner? Was there pudding? Did you get some?
guard/remark: Saved a banquet, did you? Nobody ever saves me a pudding.
gossip: Hell-rats in Evil Dave's cellar, they say. Took all the spices.
A fortune-teller froze the Duke's whole table in time, they say.
The goblin generals agreed on something at last. A dish called slop.
I hear that castle cook needed help again. Same cook. Same castle.
kid/compliment: You fought a banana demon? Was it squishy? Did you eat it after?
kid/remark: There's an evil chicken in a cave, Mum says. I want to see it!
goblin/gossip: Me hear generals eat same slop at human feast. Grey slop. Both eat it!
Human feast in Lumbridge, they say. Generals go. Only one chair.
troll/gossip: Big human feast in Lumbridge, me hear. Nobody invite trolls. Rude.
barbarian/gossip: The Duke's table frozen in time, they say. Our meat's never frozen.
A Lumbridge feast got attacked, I hear. At last, a feast worth it.

gossip: Dragons are stirring again. The Myths' Guild is asking for help.
Alec Kincade wants to know where dragons come from. Odd hobby.
Some scholar by the Myths' Guild is asking about Crandor, I hear.
The Myths' Guild won't let just anyone in, they say. Dragons first.
A fellow at the Myths' Guild has spent half his life on dragons.
pirate/gossip: Dragons over the sea again. Bad for shipping, that. Arr.
fremennik/gossip: Dragons stirring in the northern seas. Sharpen your axe.
remark: Nobody's asked why Elvarg burned Crandor, you know. Just that she did.
Elvarg's dead, and still folk whisper about where dragons come from.
goblin/gossip: Dragons stirring, humans say. Dragon just big lizard. Goblins laugh.
troll/gossip: Dragons stirring, humans say. Dragon just big lizard. Big dinner.
barbarian/gossip: Dragons stirring, city folk say. Good. A dragon is a proper fight.

compliment: Word is you saw off Galvek. I'd buy you a pint.
King Roald called the kingdoms together on your word. On your word.
The Myths' Guild took you in, I hear. They don't take just anyone.
Galvek's maker burned by his own dragon, and you stood right there.
A dragon built to end the world, they say, and you faced it.
insult: Did for Galvek, did you? You'd never know to look at you.
Slew Galvek, they say. And here you are, waiting about like anyone.
Galvek, done for. You'd think they'd have given you a bigger hat.
remark: Has the Myths' Guild put your statue up yet? They ought to.
Crandor's still a ruin, Galvek or no. Some things don't come back.
Elvarg was only the first of them, they say. The first! Ye gods.
fremennik/insult: Four fleets sailed for Ungael. Count the ships that came back.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye faced Galvek at sea and lived? Drinks are on me. One drink.
pirate/remark: Ships burning off Ungael, they say. Arr, I'd have stayed in port.
rough/compliment: Ye did for Galvek? Blimey. Ye don't look it. Meant kindly.
barkeep/compliment: You did for Galvek? Pint's on the house. Just the one, mind.
dwarf/compliment: Galvek, done for. By Guthix. Whoever forged your blade did you proud.
fremennik/compliment: Brundt sailed for Ungael with you. He speaks of it. That's rare.
kid/compliment: You fought Galvek? A dragon that big? Were you scared?
Did Galvek's fire make the sea go hot? Could you swim in it after?
guard/remark: Dragon slayer or not, that weapon stays sheathed in town.
heartland/compliment: Hang on. You're the one who did for Galvek? Blimey.
gossip: The dragonkin made Elvarg, they say. Made her, like a nail.
Four kingdoms' ships sailed from Rellekka, they say. One little dock.
The Wise Old Man went to Ungael, I hear. Fought a red dragon on deck.
Word is some of Varrock's guard never came home from Ungael.
A cat's grave in Burthorpe, they say, and folk who mourn it.
kid/remark: A cat fought a dragon, they say. My cat only fights the broom.
goblin/gossip: Galvek dragon dead, they say. Big High War God like that. War good.
Human kings all meet in one place, me hear. Goblins not invited. Rude.
troll/gossip: Human kill Galvek dragon, me hear. Dragons breathe fire. Good it dead.
Ships sail from fur town after dragon, me hear. Trolls stay. We sink.
barbarian/gossip: A dragon called Galvek, slain, they say. A saga for the longhall.
Ships sailed from Rellekka to fight dragons, I hear. Our cousins!

gossip: Trouble in the elf lands again. Lletya's sent for help, I'm told.
Still a wall through Ardougne, and still nobody says why.
Ardougne's locked up a woman for saying the plague's a lie.
Edmond's girl is in the Ardougne cells, they say. For speaking out.
Mourners still walk West Ardougne, and nobody can name one sick man.
The elves in Isafdar are at each other's throats again, I hear.
Lord Iorwerth wants his Dark Lord back, they say. Whatever that is.
guard/gossip: Woman locked up for saying the plague's a lie. Orders are orders.
remark: Something's stirring under West Ardougne, they say. Under it.
King Lathas keeps the wall up and his reasons to himself.
goblin/gossip: Tall people with biting blades have trouble, they say. Elves. Good.
troll/gossip: Trouble in elf lands, humans say. Elves far away. Not troll problem.
barbarian/gossip: A wall through Ardougne, they say. City folk hide behind walls.

compliment: Word is you freed Prifddinas. The elves must adore you.
I hear you faced the Fragment of Seren and lived. I can't picture it.
Prifddinas lets humans in now, and you were first through the gate.
Ardougne's rid of Lathas, and folk say your name when they tell it.
Into the elf lands a stranger, out of them a legend, they say.
insult: Freed Prifddinas, I hear. And still not a word of elvish.
Freed Prifddinas, they say. You'll be wanting a crystal medal.
Toppled a king and an elf lord. Try not to do it here.
remark: Prifddinas is lovely this time of year, I hear.
The plague in West Ardougne was a lie all along. Years of it. A lie.
guard/gossip: New king in Ardougne. New orders, same gates.
gossip: Ardougne's own folk sentenced Lathas, they say. Then the executioner.
A piece of the elves' own goddess was shut in a temple, they say. Was.
Word is Lord Iorwerth was shot by one of his own kind at the end.
Arianwyn the elf is out wandering the world, they say. Making amends.
A woman they'd locked up started the Ardougne Resistance, they say.
West Ardougne's wall hid a dig all along, they say. Not a plague.
kid/compliment: Is it true the elf city grew like a plant? Did you water it?
kid/remark: Mum says the Ardougne plague was pretend. I'm not allowed to pretend.
goblin/gossip: Human king chopped by own people, me hear. Goblins only argue.
troll/gossip: Human king chopped by own people, me hear. Trolls just pick biggest.
barbarian/gossip: The elves have their crystal city back, they say. Glass walls. Soft.
Ardougne's king answered for his lies, they say. Good.

gossip: Glough's up to no good again, they say. The gnomes need a hand.
Did you hear? Glough's got loose. The gnomes are in a right state.
Glough slipped his guards, they say. Nobody knows how. Or who helped.
King Narnode's sent word for the one who stopped Glough last time.
Glough's house stands empty, they say, and the king wants it searched.
remark: A gnome who hates humans, loose with a grudge. Sleep well.
Glough tried a tree, then an army. The third go is what worries me.
goblin/gossip: Gnome Glough loose again, they say. He hate humans too. Me like him.
troll/gossip: Gnome called Glough loose again, me hear. Gnome small. Not even snack.
barbarian/gossip: That gnome Glough slipped his guards again, they say. Gnomes! Hah!

compliment: I hear you stopped Glough's gorilla army. Blimey.
Word is you sorted Glough out for good. The gnomes can breathe again.
The monkey king came to the gnomes for peace, and you stood witness.
A troll and an ogre backed out of that war after a word from you.
Nieve fell in that cavern, they say, and you carried on. Fair play.
insult: Stopped Glough's army, they say. You look like you need a sit-down.
Stopped Glough, I hear. You don't look like someone who stops things.
Glough's beaten and the gnomes are safe. No parade for you, though.
remark: Glough's gone, and the Grand Tree's still standing. Good.
Glough's gone, and Nieve with him. Not a cheap victory, that.
Monkeys and gnomes at peace. My grandmother would never believe it.
gnome/remark: The Tree's still standing. That's twice we owe a human.
kid/compliment: You fought a gorilla army? How many? Was it a hundred?
Did you really ride a gorilla? Can I ride one? A small one?
guard/remark: Gorilla army, they say. We've had worse. Goblins, mostly.
gossip: Glough drank something and became a monster, they say. Not a saying.
Word is a gnome called Le Smith helped Glough slip his guards.
Awowogei stripped Kruk of his rank, they say. Bit late. Kruk was dead.
Glough bred gorillas under Ape Atoll, they say. Big ones. Angry ones.
Glough's flying ship came down north of the Gnome Stronghold, I hear.
kid/remark: A ship that flies! Glough had a ship that flies! I want one!
goblin/gossip: Glough drink potion, turn into big monster, they say. Lose anyway.
troll/gossip: Gnome drink potion, turn into big monster, me hear. Still lose. Hah.
Kob went to gnome war talks, me hear. Kob come back. Kob not say much.
barbarian/gossip: Glough drank a potion and grew into a monster, they say. Still lost.

gossip: Old ruins in the desert are stirring. Somebody ought to look.
Diggers in the desert found a door nobody can open.
A sealed vault north of Nardah, they say. Old magic on the door.
Treasure hunters are drifting toward Nardah again, I hear.
The Exam Centre lot are excited about something. They won't say what.
remark: Old empires don't stay buried. Someone always goes digging.
Doors built to stay shut don't open for nothing. Somebody will try.
goblin/gossip: Diggers find door in desert nobody can open, they say. Hit it harder.
troll/gossip: Diggers find door in desert nobody open, me hear. Trolls use rocks.
barbarian/gossip: A sealed vault in the desert, they say. Give me an axe and a day.

compliment: Vardorvis and the Whisperer, I hear. I struggle with wasps.
I hear you went into the Scar after the Leviathan. Ye gods, the Scar.
Under the salt mines at Weiss and back with your wits, they say.
You faced a thing called the Whisperer, I hear. I'd not have stayed.
A duke of the old empire, and you put him down. Ye gods.
heartland/insult: Four ancient horrors, I hear. And here you are, out for a stroll.
insult: Slew the Leviathan, they say. Mind the puddle.
Vardorvis, a duke, a leviathan, a whisperer. Still no title, though.
remark: Half the Mahjarrat waited for someone to open that vault, they say.
gossip: Dr Banikan from the Digsite was a Mahjarrat the whole time, they say.
There's a wood past Kebos where the trees get into you, they say.
Word is the Mahjarrat are squabbling again. Sliske's name comes up.
Ancient things under Camdozaal, they say. A whole sunken city.
A Mahjarrat wore a human face all along, they say. Nobody noticed.
kid/compliment: Did the Leviathan have a hundred teeth? Did you count? You should've.
kid/remark: Dad says there's a whispering thing underground. I whisper back.
goblin/gossip: Human kill leviathan in desert, me hear. Big fish. Big dinner.
troll/gossip: Human fight big leviathan thing, me hear. Trolls stay out of water.
Big old thing under Weiss, me hear. Human went down. Trolls stay up.
barbarian/gossip: A Digsite scholar turned out a Mahjarrat, they say. Magic folk. Bah!
Some beast under the sea by the desert, slain, I hear. A big fish!

gossip: Some old heroes have been sent for. Something's up, mark my words.
The Taverley druids are asking after seasoned adventurers. Quietly.
A messenger of Armadyl's been handing out letters, they say. Sealed.
Word is the Mahjarrat are stirring. Nobody says that word lightly.
remark: The druids look worried. Druids don't look worried. That worries me.
goblin/gossip: Druids want old heroes, they say. Goblins not asked. Goblins mighty!
troll/gossip: Druids want old heroes, me hear. Trolls not asked. Trolls never asked.
barbarian/gossip: The druids are sending for old heroes, they say. Nobody sent for us.

compliment: Word is you stood against Lucien. Not many can say that.
I hear you've seen Guthix's own cave. Fair play.
Druids, knights and Armadyl's own stood together. Your doing, I hear.
You found what Guthix buried. Not many have laid eyes on it, they say.
You touched the Stone of Jas and walked away, they say. Walked away!
insult: I hear Lucien got away. Not your fault. Probably.
Found the Stone of Jas, I hear. Then Lucien found it. Pity, that.
Lucien's got the Stone, and you've got a story. Fair exchange?
gossip: They say Lucien's loose with something he oughtn't have.
Did you hear? Lucien has the Staff of Armadyl and the Stone both now.
They say the Dark Squall was Surok Magis all along. The Varrock one.
Lucien raised dead heroes to serve him, they say. In the Wilderness.
Sloane of the Warriors' Guild never came home, they say. Lucien.
The slayer master at Shilo is dead, they say. Lucien. One spell.
A man called Movario hunted that Stone for Lucien, they say.
rough/compliment: Ye stood against Lucien? Cor. I'd not have. Honest.
fremennik/compliment: Lucien, and you walked away. Hah! The spirits favour you, outerlander.
kid/remark: Lucien's the scary one, right? Dad goes quiet when I ask.
Lucien's got a magic rock, I heard. I've got a rock. Mine's not magic.
guard/remark: Lucien's above my rank. Move along, and good luck to you.
remark: Guthix hid that Stone for a reason, they say. Lucien's not the reason.
The Stone of Jas made the Wilderness, they say. In Zamorak's hands.
kid/compliment: You touched the Stone of Jas? Did it make you strong? Lift me up!
goblin/gossip: Lucien get magic rock, they say. Big High War God not need rock.
troll/gossip: Lucien got big magic rock, me hear. Trolls got rocks too. Not magic.
barbarian/gossip: Lucien's got a staff and a stone now, they say. Wizard's weapons. Bah!

gossip: Glough's gone for good this time. The cavern saw to that.
Steve's taken Nieve's post. Big boots. He knows it.
Awowogei came to the Stronghold himself. Himself! Peace, they say.
Glough drank his own brew and brought the cave down on himself.
Marim's taking visitors now, would you believe. Monkeys and all.
compliment: You're the human from the crash site? Narnode speaks highly of you.
Are you the human who stood with Nieve? I'm... sorry.
Glough's gorillas, and you still standing. Narnode's beside himself.
insult: Glough warned us about humans. Funny how they keep turning up.
plain/insult: Nieve fell. You walked out. Nobody here's quite forgiven that.
gnome/compliment: You stood with Nieve at the cavern? Every gnome here knows your name.
gnome/insult: Glough was one of ours. We'd have liked to deal with him ourselves.
kid/remark: Nieve's grave is up by the crash site. I put a flower on it.

gossip: Glough's slipped house arrest. Nobody slips house arrest on their own.
Narnode's doubled the watch on the Grand Tree. Won't say why.
Galvek's dead, but there's still dragons in that old fort. Mind.
They say a cat died at Ungael saving a human. A cat!
Dallas Jones never came back from Lithkren. Poor man.
Bob the cat was Robert the Strong all along. That cat!
compliment: Are you the one who faced Galvek? Four kingdoms owe you.
You're the one who gave Bob his memories back? Robert the Strong!
plain/insult: Bob went to Ungael for you. Bob didn't come back. You did.
Galvek's dead. So are Dallas and the cat. Nobody's cheering here.
kid/remark: A cat died saving you, they say. A cat. Did you say thank you?

gossip: That old ruin on the hill. Nobody goes near it. Nobody should.
Prifddinas is back. Grown from a seed, they say. A seed!
Iestin leads the Iorwerth now. Half the city still watches them.
Lathas is dead and Thoros is king. Ardougne cheered. Loudly.
Baxtorian's free of the stone and an elder now. After all this time.
Lathas hid in a wardrobe, they say. A king! In a wardrobe!
compliment: You're the human who walked the Temple of Light and came back?
Wait. You're the one Baxtorian speaks of? He speaks of few.
You were there when Prifddinas grew back? What was it like?
plain/insult: Lord Iorwerth wanted Seren home. You wanted a city. You got yours.
Eight clans and one human. Guess who the songs are about.
One human, one Fragment, and now everyone's an expert on elves.
King Tyras burned in his own camp. Odd, you being there that day.

gossip: The mourners dig under Ardougne, and Lletya waits. Always waits.
Iorwerth's scouts were in the forest again. Keep off the paths.
Lletya's scouts are out east again. Something's coming.
That Smith fellow from the dig? Wasn't a Smith at all, they say.
The Vault's open. Whatever was in it has gone north.
The Stranglewood's gone quiet. Nobody's asking why.
compliment: The Scar, and you walked back out of it. I'd not have gone in.
You went into the Stranglewood and came out? Most don't.
plain/insult: You opened a door even the Mahjarrat couldn't. Proud of that?
Sliske had you running errands in a borrowed face. Did you not notice?
remark: Vardorvis gives me nightmares, and I've only heard the stories.

gossip: Diggers at the Vault keep failing the door. Good. Leave it shut.
Lucien has the Stone. Nobody says where. Nobody says much.
Hazelmere's gone. Lucien turned him to ash, they say.
A gnome's on the Warriors' Guild door now. Ghommal won't be back.
Turael's gone. Burthorpe's had to find a new slayer master.
compliment: You were at that temple in the Wilderness? Then you saw them fall.
You're the one Thaerisk speaks of. He doesn't say it lightly.
You found the Stone of Jas? Before Lucien got his hands on it?
plain/insult: Six heroes died at that temple. You came home. Nobody's sure how.
The best of us went in with you. We buried what came out.
Lucien walked off with the Stone. Some rescue that was.

gossip: Ivy's been asking after anyone who can hold a sword. Urgently.
The Taverley druids are up to something. Thaerisk won't say what.
Strange folk in Burthorpe asking after the old heroes. Worrying.
Lord Drakan's dead. Did you hear? Morytania's never been so quiet.
The vampyres have a new lord, a Vitur, they say. He wants peace.
Drakan killed one of his own lords in front of everyone, they say.
Efaritay, queen of old Hallowvale, is alive, they say. Still.
Word is Drakan wanted all vampyres back in their old world. To hunt.
Folk called aranei died for a vampyre in Vampyrium, they say.
compliment: You're the one who did for Lord Drakan? You look so... ordinary.
Is it true you've been to Vampyrium and back?
The blood moon rose over Morytania, then Drakan fell. That was you.
Word is you took Drakan's own spear off him at the end. And kept it.
The vampyres' own world and back? And here you are, calm as milk.
barkeep/compliment: You're the one who did for Drakan? Sit down, love. Anything you like.
kid/compliment: You killed Lord Drakan? The real one? Did you use a stake?
Is Lord Drakan really dead? Did he go to dust? Did you keep any?
guard/remark: Drakan's dead, they say. Doesn't shorten my shift.
insult: Did for Drakan, they say. Centuries he lasted. Decent effort.
Slew Drakan, they say. I'd have expected more teeth marks.
remark: A vampyre lord dead and the moon back to its usual colour. Good.
Misthalin's been told there'll be no war from the east, I hear.
kid/remark: The moon went red, they say. I looked. It was just the moon.
goblin/gossip: Drakan dead, me hear. Red moon over swamp land. Goblins stay home.
troll/gossip: Vampyre lord dead in swamp land, me hear. Vampyres only drink. Waste.
barbarian/gossip: Lord Drakan's dead, I hear. A vampyre lord. Now that was a fight.

gossip: They say the Vitur fellow's outlawed the tithe. Some vyres sulk.
Half of Meiyerditch is packing for the Salve. Can't blame them.
Veliaf's reopened the pub in Burgh de Rott. Myreque's Rest.
Efaritay's selling vampyrebane blades in Castle Drakan now. Imagine.
The Vyrewatch let some adventurer walk right past. Didn't blink.
Safalaan's gone to Vampyrium, the story goes. Won't forgive Vanescula.
compliment: Drakan's roof. Up and down again. That was you, they're saying.
You stood with Queen Efaritay against Drakan? Saradomin bless you.
shady/insult: Centuries of order undone by a mortal. How very quaint.
Enjoy the quiet, hero. Some of us preferred the old ways.
The tithe kept order. Now everyone's just... free. Ghastly.
Drakan ruled for centuries. You're a footnote with a flail.
burgher/gossip: Vitur fellow says no more tithe. Hope he can read his own notice.
burgher/compliment: You done for Drakan? Proper? I'll tell me mum.

gossip: Another Blood Moon festival, they say. Lock your doors. Or don't.
Something's been moving under the castle. Tunnels, they whisper.
Safalaan's still in Drakan's hands, and Veliaf's gone quiet about it.
burgher/gossip: Blood Moon coming, they say. Don't need to read to know that's bad.

gossip: The Myreque are finished, folk reckon. Castle Drakan still stands.
Vanstrom Klause is gone. Burgh de Rott had a quiet drink about it.
Lord Drakan burnt half the Myreque in his own courtyard, I'm told.
compliment: Into Darkmeyer and out again, and still with a pulse. Remarkable.
You're the one who stopped Slepe's sickness spreading? Bless you.
plain/insult: You took the Myreque to Castle Drakan. Veliaf doesn't talk about it.
Plotting with Vanescula Drakan, were you? Lovely company you keep.
burgher/gossip: The Myreque went off to the castle. Fewer came back.

gossip: Plague in Slepe again. Nobody goes near the place.
Veliaf's gone to Slepe. Something about the sickness, he said.
Slepe's sickness is spreading. Nobody's found a cure. Nobody's close.
Something's wrong with Lady Verzik. Something with more legs.
Lady Verzik died long ago, they whisper. So who's on the stage?
compliment: You've been in the Theatre and out again? Most only manage in.
You've seen what's really on that stage? Brave soul.
plain/insult: Spoiling the Lady's shows. Sinhaza had so few pleasures.
The Theatre had a perfectly good name until you went in.

gossip: The Lady's recruiting for her show. Nobody plays twice.
Sinhaza's been quiet. Too quiet. The Lady's planning something.
Brumty's sheep came up all colours, they say. Plague, he called it.
Someone got inside the mourners' place. And out again, which is new.
compliment: You're the one who got inside the mourners' headquarters?
Word is you saw through the mourners' plague. Clever, that.
plain/insult: West Ardougne took sick on bad grain. Some say you helped.

gossip: The Temple of Light's lit again, I hear. Whatever that means.
Someone went all the way down to the Death Altar. Down there!
compliment: You've been to the Temple of Light? And found your way out?

gossip: Someone let a Mahjarrat out of the pyramid. Just let him out.
compliment: You're the one who found all four diamonds? Clever, that.
Four guardians, four diamonds, and you still standing? Blimey.
plain/insult: Freed something ancient from a pyramid. I'm sure it's grateful.
You let a Mahjarrat loose for some spells. Fair trade, was it?

gossip: Some archaeologist at the Bedabin Camp wants diamonds. Odd sort.
The bandits say something's buried under the desert. Something old.
Sophanem's pox has lifted. Menaphos says it'll open. Says.
The Champion of Scabaras is dead. The beetles have been sulking since.
compliment: You're the adventurer from Ullek? The High Priest prays for you.
You fetched the Lily of the Elid for Sophanem? Zahur says so.
plain/insult: Menaphos says it'll open its gates. For you? I'd not hold my breath.
Zahur did the brewing. You carried a flower. Very pretty, I'm sure.

gossip: Sophanem's sick again and Menaphos has bolted its gates. Again.
There's a sickness in Sophanem the healers can't name.
The Moons are sealed below again. Eyatlalli saw to the ritual.
compliment: You went down under Cam Torum? I'd not go for all the gold in it.
You helped Eyatlalli with the Moons? Cam Torum sleeps easier.
dwarf/compliment: You went under Cam Torum for the Moons? Brave, for one so tall.

gossip: The Teokan of Ranul was the Augur all along. All along!
Furia Tullus is in a cell. The Prince spoke for her, they say.
Ennius Tullus is dead. The Queen herself was there.
Teumo's name's not spoken in Cam Torum now, they say. Not once.
compliment: They say you walked into the cult beside the Prince. In robes!
Wait. The Prince gave you his grandfather's blade? You're the one.
You stood beside the Queen against Ennius? That's the story.
plain/insult: The Dawn still comes, friend. You only delayed the sun.
Metzli lied, they say. As if the palace has ever done otherwise.
The Augur's dead. The faith isn't. You can't stab a sunrise.
dwarf/remark: Teumo sold out Cam Torum, they say. Dwarves don't forget. Or forgive.

gossip: Emissaries preaching in the market again. Nobody stops them.
The Prince is missing, they say. Taken by the Emissaries.
King Hosidius, crowned and killed the same day. Artur rules now.
The Council's in irons. Andrews and Unkar, awaiting trial.
Poor Rose. Twenty years in a shack, and no cure at the end.
compliment: You're the one who fought that demon out at Molch? Brave.
Wait, you helped Martin Holt bring down the Council?
plain/insult: Lord Shayzien stepped aside for Hosidius. Look how that ended.
The houses squabbled under the Council. Now under a king. Progress.

gossip: Martin Holt's shouting outside the castle again. Guards don't move.
The King's daughter went mad, the Council says. Convenient, that.
West Ardougne's still walled off. Plague, the mourners say.
The dwarves at Cam Torum say the Moons are restless below.
Druids whisper about Lucien. Druids don't whisper for nothing.
They say Lucien grows bolder. Someone ought to worry.

compliment: The hooded fellow in the pub's asking after brave sorts. That's you.
The stranger in the pub wants weapons carried. You've the arms for it.
insult: The hooded chap's still waiting on his steel. Shops sell it, you know.
plain/insult: Freedom fighters in the swamp, and you in the pub. Sounds right.
remark: That hooded fellow's been nursing the same seat for days.
gossip: Some call the Myreque freedom fighters. Others say terrorists.
Rebels hiding in the myre, they say. Hidden in the myre, even.
Strangers asking about the Myreque in the pub. Eyes everywhere, mind.
starter/compliment: Hello there. Vanstrom Klause. You look the heroic sort, stranger.
Bring the weapons back to me and I'll give you a nice surprise.
starter/insult: Any luck finding the Myreque? No? Shame. I'd so love to meet them.
starter/remark: The Myreque... real meat and drink of high adventure. So they say.

compliment: You're the one who saw off that hellhound in the Hollows? Blimey.
Word is you stood your ground when that hellhound came. Fair play.
insult: Six swords into a swamp, I hear. Not so much as a thank-you, I'd bet.
plain/insult: Led Vanstrom right to the Myreque's door, they say. Good of you.
remark: That hooded fellow's gone from the pub. Someone else has his chair.
gossip: Sani Piliu's dead. And Harold Evans. Vanstrom's work, all of it.
Vanstrom was a vampyre all along. Sat in our pub, bold as brass.
The Myreque have left the Hollows. Vanstrom knows the place, see.
starter/compliment: Hello friend! Not Vanstrom, before you ask. Just a man with a chair.
starter/insult: You looked ready to run me through. I'm not him, you know.
starter/remark: Steady on. You've a score to settle with someone. Not me, I hope.

compliment: Veliaf's looking for a new hideout. You've a nose for places, friend.
Burgh de Rott, Veliaf says. Someone brave needs to go first.
insult: We need a new hideout. You look like you've slept in worse. Any ideas?
plain/insult: Vanstrom knows this cave. Standing about in it isn't a plan.
remark: Vanstrom knows where we are. Every creak sounds like a vyre.
gossip: Veliaf says Burgh de Rott's full of folk who fled Meiyerditch.
Ivan's not slept since Sani. None of us have, really.
Silver, Veliaf says. Take silver if you're going near a vampyre.
starter/compliment: Well met, friend. We need a new hideout, and you've the legs for it.
starter/insult: Well met. Burgh de Rott, and take silver. Don't lead anyone to us.
starter/remark: We're really not that organised. Vanstrom proved as much.

compliment: You're the one who put Gadderanks down? Nobody here mourns him.
Aurel's shop, the bank, the furnace. All you, they say. Bless you.
insult: I hear you fixed the shop and the tithe men turned up. Funny, that.
plain/insult: You lit the furnace. Vanstrom smelt the smoke. Cosy, was it?
remark: Cornelius is a banker now. Never thought I'd see it in Burgh de Rott.
gossip: Gadderanks is dead. Begged for his family at the end, I'm told.
The Myreque are under the inn now. Don't tell anyone I said so.
Young Ivan's gone to the priest at the Salve. Safer, Veliaf says.
burgher/compliment: Fixed up the village, you did. A shop! A bank! Whatever that is.
burgher/gossip: Got a furnace now. Nobody knows what to put in it.
burgher/remark: Gadderanks is gone. Can't say I'll miss him.

compliment: Veliaf wants word from Meiyerditch. You've been through worse, friend.
Someone has to get round that wall. Veliaf thinks it's you.
insult: Meiyerditch is east. The boat's south. Neither's in this cellar.
plain/insult: The Sanguinesti lot might be dead. Standing here won't tell us.
remark: Nobody's heard from the Sanguinesti in an age.
gossip: The Vyrewatch can't be killed, Veliaf says. Not even with the rod.
A wall round Meiyerditch, and a boat round the wall. A rotten one.
Humans are farmed in Meiyerditch, they say. Like cattle.
starter/compliment: Well met, friend. What news? None? Then I've a job for you.
starter/insult: Meiyerditch, east. Take precautions. You know, this time.
starter/remark: Even the Rod of Ivandis does nothing to the Vyrewatch. Nothing.

compliment: The Sanguinesti are alive? Veliaf hasn't smiled like that in years.
Private, is it? Safalaan doesn't recommend just anyone.
insult: Drew three pictures of a castle, I hear. The vampyres loved them.
plain/insult: Vanstrom put you on the floor. Vanescula's servant saved you.
remark: Roald sent his regards and no soldiers. Edicts, apparently.
gossip: Werewolves crossing the Salve for tithes, if you please. The Salve!
Safalaan's alive and sketching Castle Drakan. Brave or daft.
Vanescula Drakan's taken an interest in Safalaan, they whisper.
starter/compliment: Well met, Private. Safalaan speaks well of you. Myreque prevail.
starter/insult: So Roald sent no troops. Did you beg? I did say beg.
starter/remark: This war is far from over. Plenty of time to contribute.

compliment: Garth tells a fine tale about Serafina. Worth a listen, friend.
You've the look of someone who might survive the Theatre. Few do.
insult: Thousands tried the Theatre. One came out. Don't get ideas.
plain/insult: You're not here for the tithe, are you? You've the pallor for it.
remark: Serafina. Everyone here knows the name. Nobody knows where she went.
gossip: The Lady promises freedom to any who survive her Theatre. Any.
Blood tithes by sector. So nobody runs out all at once.
Garth's told the Serafina story so often the guards mouth along.
starter/compliment: Hello there! Interested in the tale of Serafina? You'd like it.
starter/insult: The tale of Serafina? It's long. You look like you've the time.
starter/remark: Only one person ever survived the Theatre. Only one.

compliment: You're the one who killed Ranis Drakan? With a flail? Ye gods.
The Slayer, they call you now. The whole city heard your speech.
insult: Killed a Drakan on the castle steps. Subtle. Very subtle.
plain/insult: Half the Sanguinesti died for those notes. You kept the flail.
shady/insult: Ranis kept the tithes orderly. Now the cattle think they can bite.
A human with a flail. Lord Drakan will be so very amused.
remark: Ranis dead on the castle steps, and not a word from the castle since.
gossip: Ranis Drakan is dead. Killed by a human, in front of everyone.
Serafina never left, they whisper. She's still in that Theatre.
Flaygian, Mekritus, Andiess. The Myreque lost three in one night.
starter/compliment: I used to tell the tale of Serafina. Now they ask for yours.
starter/insult: Careful talking of the Myreque round here. It gets you in trouble.
starter/remark: Nothing's been seen of Lord Drakan in years. Vanescula, now and then.

compliment: Edmond's girl went over the wall three weeks back. Help him, friend.
Edmond's been digging in his garden for days. He could use a hand.
insult: Edmond's daughter is still over that wall. Not that it's your wall.
plain/insult: West Ardougne's walled off. So far it's kept you out beautifully.
remark: They say there's plague behind that wall. Nobody says what kind.
gossip: Edmond's Elena is a healer. Went west to help, never came back.
The mourners run West Ardougne now. Masks and all.
They blame King Tyras for the plague over there. Came back with it.
starter/compliment: You'd help? Elena crossed the wall to heal them and never came back.
starter/insult: Sorry, I can't stop to talk. Unless you've a spade. Have you a spade?
starter/remark: The soil's rock hard... buckets of water... that grill in the sewer...

compliment: You're the one who got Elena out of West Ardougne? Bless you.
Word is you dug through Edmond's garden and into the sewers. Clever.
insult: I hear you brewed a hangover cure for the warder. Hero of Ardougne.
plain/insult: Crawled through a sewer in a gas mask for a girl you'd never met. Odd.
remark: Edmond's garden's never been the same. He doesn't mind.
gossip: Elena's home. Walked in the front door before her rescuer did.
A black cross on the door means plague. Or kidnappers, it turns out.
Bravek signed a warrant for the plague house. Hungover, mind.
starter/compliment: Ah, hello! Thank you again for rescuing my daughter.
starter/insult: Elena beat you back by minutes, you know. Minutes.
starter/remark: The sewer passage closed up after you. Probably for the best.

compliment: Elena has plague samples and nothing to test them with. Help her?
Elena needs her distillator back off the mourners. You've the nerve.
insult: Elena's waiting on her equipment. The mourners aren't posting it.
plain/insult: Elena wants a distillator fetched. You don't know what one is, do you?
remark: Elena's been shut in with her samples since she got back.
gossip: The mourners took Elena's equipment. For 'safety', they said.
Jerico keeps pigeons by the wall. Odd hobby for odd times.
Elena wants to test that plague herself. The mourners said no.
starter/compliment: Hey! Thanks again for freeing me. Now, about my distillator...
starter/insult: Being kidnapped was inconvenient. Don't be. Fetch my distillator.
starter/remark: I can't test a single sample without that distillator.

compliment: Word is you got Elena's kit back off the mourners. Good on you.
Into the mourners' headquarters dressed as a doctor? Some nerve!
insult: Put a rotten apple in the mourners' stew, I hear. Child's play.
plain/insult: Ran three vials to Varrock in a priest's robe. Very holy of you.
remark: Elena keeps saying she wishes she knew what's going on over there.
gossip: The west gate opens for some now, they say. Friends of the King.
The mourners had a stomach upset. Bad stew, they say.
Elena's distillator is back. The mourners say nothing about it.
starter/compliment: Hey! Now I can finally run these tests. Thank you.
starter/insult: The touch paper didn't change. Nothing. Try not to look so pleased.
starter/remark: Even without the plague, I still worry about the people over there.

compliment: The King wants a way west through the pass. You look sure-footed.
Lathas needs the pass crossed. His best soldiers didn't manage it.
insult: The pass is still shut. Soldiers fell in there. You've a warm pub.
sharp/insult: The King asked for a warrior. He's making do with you, citizen.
remark: Cultists in the pass now, they say. As if it weren't bad enough.
gossip: Some of the King's best men went into the pass and didn't come back.
King Tyras is gathering strength out west, the palace says.
The King's tracker, Koftik, is waiting at the pass. Poor man.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer. I assume you're here about my brother? Splendid.
starter/insult: The pass has swallowed my best soldiers. I'm sure you'll be fine.
starter/remark: My brother gathers strength in the west. A way through must be found.

compliment: Word is you did for Iban. Called himself Zamorak's son, you know.
You found the way west through the pass? The King's delighted.
insult: I hear you dropped a doll down a well and called it a victory.
sharp/insult: Three paladins went in with you. Only you came out. Interesting.
remark: Koftik's himself again, they say. Can't remember a thing.
gossip: Iban is dead, I'm told. The temple came down on top of him.
The King's men are building a well in the pass. A Well of Voyage.
There's a witch in that pass still, the soldiers say. With a cat.
starter/compliment: Incredible, adventurer. A true warrior. Your loyalty inspires us all.
starter/insult: Iban's gone. My brother isn't. Don't get comfortable, adventurer.
starter/remark: Once the Well is finished, we move against my brother at last.

compliment: The King's sending someone west through the Well. Someone with nerve.
Lathas has elves waiting for his envoy out west, they say. That's you.
insult: The King's errand is still waiting. The Well's not going anywhere.
sharp/insult: Lord Iorwerth's expecting someone impressive. Do break it gently.
remark: Elves. The King says there are elves out west. Elves!
gossip: King Tyras is west with an army, the palace says. It wants him gone.
An elf lord has offered King Lathas his full support. An elf lord!
Tirannwn, they call it. Elf country. Full of traps, I hear.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Through the Well. Lord Iorwerth's elves will meet you.
starter/insult: Leave me, citizen. I'm far too busy. Oh, it's you. Well, go on then.
starter/remark: My brother... the Dark Lord... it all ends in the west.

compliment: Word is you crossed Tirannwn and lived. The traps alone, ye gods.
The King's very pleased with you, they say. Very pleased indeed.
insult: I hear you blew up a king's tent with a barrel. Diplomacy, that.
sharp/insult: You killed a king because another king asked. Did you check which?
remark: King Tyras is dead, and the wall's still up. Odd, that.
gossip: A flying fireball did for King Tyras, the story goes. A fireball!
The plague must remain, the palace says. Even now. Even now.
The elves out west are at war among themselves, I'm told. Elves!
starter/compliment: Well done. You've done an excellent job. This will do nicely.
starter/insult: Hello. I've got nothing for you right now. Do stop hovering.
starter/remark: Even with my brother gone, the plague must remain. For now.

compliment: Maybe this human isn't as bad as Islwyn thinks.
Arianwyn said a human might come. Islwyn's not happy about it.
insult: You're the human that killed Tyras? Islwyn won't want to hear it.
plain/insult: All you humans do is take and destroy, Islwyn says. Prove him wrong.
remark: Islwyn's grandmother was Glarial, you know. The queen.
gossip: Arianwyn's told the forest about the one who killed Tyras.
Islwyn's bows are crystal. Far superior to human work, he says.
starter/compliment: Very well, human. There's something you must do first.
starter/insult: All you humans do is take and destroy. We don't need your help.
starter/remark: It was humans that led to my grandmother's death. Humans.

compliment: You consecrated Glarial's tomb? Islwyn admits he was wrong. Islwyn!
Crystal from Islwyn's own stock? He doesn't give that to anyone.
insult: Killed a moss guardian for a seed, I hear. The moss is furious.
plain/insult: Planted a seed by a waterfall and the elves forgave you. Easy, that.
remark: Glarial rests under the falls now, properly. Good.
gossip: Islwyn says the human showed care and compassion. His words.
Eluned's taking the human to Lletya. To Arianwyn himself.
Ilfeen will re-chant crystal if you find her in the forest.
starter/compliment: Ahh, good to see you back. After more crystal equipment?
starter/insult: I admit I was wrong about you. Don't make me say it twice.
starter/remark: My grandmother rests under the waterfall. The perfect place.

compliment: There's a delegation from Varlamore at the palace. Go and have a look.
Alina in the square can't stop talking about Varlamore. Humour her.
insult: Foreign princes at the palace, and here's you, just standing about.
remark: The Shining Kingdom, they call it. Shut for hundreds of years.
gossip: A prince from Varlamore's at the palace, says the Herald. Knights too.
Varlamore's opening up for trade, I hear. Over the western sea.
Noah reckons a kingdom shut for centuries sounds like a prison.
starter/compliment: The delegation from Varlamore! Do you not want to be first there?
starter/insult: Varlamore! The Shining Kingdom! And you've not even heard of it?
starter/remark: Far across the western sea, over the mountains... Think of it!
heartland/insult: Varlamore's opening up, they say. Not to the likes of you, guv.

compliment: You're the one who marked out those bandits in the square? Sharp eyes.
Word is you saved that Varlamore priest from a knife. Fair play.
insult: Followed a guard round Varrock, I hear. Did he give you a sweet after?
remark: Sergeant Tobyn's been very pleased with himself lately.
gossip: Four bandits in guards' armour, arrested in the square. Imagine!
The treaty's signed, says the Herald. Varlamore's open to anyone now.
That prince was up on the palace roof asking questions, I hear.
heartland/insult: Bandits dressed as guards fooled everyone but you. Says a lot, guv.

compliment: The Prince is asking after the outsider from Varrock. That's you.
The Tullus twins want a word with you. That's an honour, round here.
insult: The Tullus twins are waiting. They don't like waiting.
plain/insult: An outsider, summoned by the Prince. The twins looked unimpressed.
remark: The Teokan of Ralos hasn't been seen since Varrock, they say.
gossip: Someone tried to kill the Teokan in Varrock. Varrock, of all places!
The twins organised the whole delegation. They'll tell you so.
The Prince is keeping his father close. Very close, the knights say.
starter/compliment: You. The Prince wishes to speak with you. Do not keep him waiting.
starter/insult: Doesn't look like much. Still, the Prince asked for you. Go.
starter/remark: We organised the whole delegation. As was our duty.

compliment: You're the outsider who rounded up all six knights? Impressive.
You held the Teomat against the cultists? May the sun light your way.
insult: Sobered up a knight at a fountain, I hear. The stuff of legend.
plain/insult: Six knights rounded up, one traitor, and the Teokan still got stabbed.
remark: Metzli's gone. Ask the priests and watch them change the subject.
gossip: Ennius Tullus executed a knight on the spot, they say. Velam.
The Teokan of Ralos was stabbed at the Teomat. He'll live, we're told.
Metzli, Teokan of Ranul, vanished the night of the attack.
starter/compliment: You've done well, outsider. The Prince will want to hear it from you.
starter/insult: What's done is done. Do not dwell on it. Or on us.
starter/remark: This is how we deal with traitors. You're in Varlamore now.

compliment: The Prince needs someone he trusts for his plan. He said your name.
Servius is on his feet again. He asks after you, they say.
insult: The Prince has a plan. Nobody likes it. You're in it.
plain/insult: The Queen wants someone the Prince trusts sent. Pity it's an outsider.
remark: The Queen was here. Nobody's seen the Prince smile since.
gossip: Cultists are recruiting out in the gorge, they whisper.
The Queen came to the Teomat herself. Words were had.
Twice someone's tried to kill the Teokan. Twice.
starter/compliment: Nilsal, my friend. I've a plan. You'll like it. Well, you won't.
starter/insult: Nilsal. You're the only one I trust now, and you're an outsider.
starter/remark: Father will recover. His would-be killers are still out there.

compliment: Into the Emissaries' tower with the Prince? I'd not have slept.
You fought a frost nagua alone in the ruins, they say. And walked out.
insult: Joined a cult in a robe, I hear. Did they at least feed you?
plain/insult: You went in with the Prince and came out without him. Careless.
remark: Servius won't bow to a knife wound, he says. Nor to anything else.
gossip: The Prince is gone. Taken from the ruins. Metzli's work, Servius says.
Metzli leads the Emissaries. Their Augur. The Teokan of Ranul herself.
The Tullus twins are Ralos and Ranul reborn, the cult says. Reborn!
Servius says they'll all burn in the light of Ralos. He means it.

compliment: The woman in that tent knows a way into Sophanem, they say. Ask nice.
That woman in the tent is waiting for someone. Might be you, friend.
insult: Sophanem's shut tight. You'll not get in by staring at it.
plain/insult: Plagues in Sophanem and you camping outside. Bold or daft, friend.
remark: Sophanem's locked down. Plagues, they say. More than one.
gossip: A new High Priest in Sophanem and plagues the same week. Odd timing.
There's a red-haired woman camped by the pyramid. Hates cats.
Desert nights are cold. That woman in the tent has no tinderbox.
starter/compliment: Hello, adventurer. A full waterskin and a tinderbox, and we'll talk.
starter/insult: You have the smell of cats about you. Filthy creatures. Keep it away.
starter/remark: These desert nights are very cold... I seem to have lost my tinderbox.

compliment: You're the one who put Klenter's jar back? The priests still talk.
You stood against the Devourer at the ceremony? Icthlarin bless you.
insult: Robbed a tomb, then put it all back, I hear. Make up your mind.
plain/insult: Stole from Klenter's pyramid under a spell, you say. Convenient spell.
remark: Klenter's ghost has gone quiet at last. Thank Icthlarin.
That cat of yours opened a pyramid door, they say. Clever puss.
gossip: That tent by the pyramid is empty. Nobody saw the woman leave.
A priest was possessed at the ceremony. He's recovered, mostly.
The pox is still with us. The new High Priest looks tired.

compliment: The High Priest wants someone who isn't afraid of Menaphos. You?
Our people are stuck in Menaphos. The High Priest could use you.
insult: Menaphos won't open its gates. Can't blame them, looking at you.
plain/insult: Not caught the plague yet? Call that your great deed so far.
remark: The bank's a hole in the ground since the beetles came up.
gossip: The High Priest took a party to the Menaphos bridge. Got shot at.
Pharaoh Kemesis leads Menaphos in a secular way, the priests sigh.
Things came up through the temple cellar before the plagues. Things.
starter/compliment: You'd really be willing to help us again? Then come, listen.
starter/insult: My focus is on the dead. You're not quite there yet, so listen.
starter/remark: Those guards are our brethren. We'll not fight them. We'll not.

compliment: You're the one who killed that giant scarab under the city? Blessings.
Our people came home from Menaphos among the dead. Your doing.
insult: Poor Jex got clubbed, I hear. Not by you, they say. Still.
plain/insult: Al Kharid's spies are all over Sophanem now. You brought one in.
remark: The bank's back under the temple. The merchants are open again.
gossip: Kaleef is dead down there. A keris still in the beast, I'm told.
Menaphos sent over its dead, and some of ours walked out of the pile!
Trade with Al Kharid now, if you please. The High Priest's not keen.
starter/compliment: Hello again. Our city of the dead is slowly coming back to life.
starter/insult: Only this infuriating pox left. No cure in your pack, I take it.
starter/remark: Menaphos stays shut till every plague is gone, they insist. Every one.

compliment: The pirate on the west dock's after company. Lunar Isle, he says.
Brundt talks of peace with the Moon Clan. It'd take someone like you.
insult: The Moon Clan have hated us for centuries. They've not met you yet.
plain/insult: Off to the Moon Clan? They do everything by magic. You'll fit in.
remark: Lokar Searunner. Half pirate, half Fremennik. All mouth.
gossip: Lokar ran off to be a pirate. Rellekka bored him, he tells everyone.
The Moon Clan do everything by magic. Won't share a word of it.
Hundreds of years at war with the Moon Clan, and still no end.
starter/compliment: Hey there! Got that seal thingy off the chief loser yet? Let's sail.
starter/insult: Don't talk to me. No time for the likes of you. ...Fine. What is it?
starter/remark: Growing crops, milking cows... So boring. That's why I left.

compliment: Brundt says you dreamed with the Moon Clan. And woke up, I see.
Brundt says there's progress with the Moon Clan at last. Your doing.
insult: I hear you had to fight yourself in a dream. Who won?
plain/insult: Made friends with the Moon Clan, did you? Keep the spells to yourself.
fremennik/insult: Back from Lunar Isle smelling of spells. Wash before the longhall.
remark: Baba Yaga's house walks about on chicken legs, they say. Walks!
gossip: The pirates' ship sailed in circles. Jinxed by a cabin boy, no less.
Brundt reckons we can really make progress with the Moon Clan now.
The Moon Clan are spreading word about an open-minded mainlander.
starter/remark: Loserville, with all the losers. And I ferry people to it. Hmph.

compliment: Mord on the north dock's looking for you. Something about the isles.
Trolls on the northern isles, they say. You'd be useful up there.
insult: Jatizso's king wants a stranger to run errands. You'll do, apparently.
plain/insult: Mord's on the dock. He's a ferryman. The boat won't come to you.
remark: Jatizso and Neitiznot. Four generations of 'is so', 'is not'.
gossip: Trolls razed Neitiznot. A whole town, gone.
Jatizso's king taxes all that moves. And some things that don't.
Mord's from Jatizso and his wife's from Neitiznot. Dinner must be fun.
starter/compliment: Hello there! Mord Gunnars, humble ferryman. Fancy seeing Jatizso?
starter/insult: I'm surprised King Sorvott wants you. Don't expect gratitude.
starter/remark: Nine days and nine nights, the full history takes. Ask Maria.

compliment: You're the one who took the Troll King's head? Neitiznot sings of you.
Burowgar gave you his own helm, they say. His own helm!
fremennik/compliment: Slayer of the Troll King! Sit by me at the longhall, brother.
insult: Collected window tax for King Sorvott, I hear. People's hero.
plain/insult: Spied in a jester's hat for Sorvott, and he still called you a liar.
remark: Sorvott still says the Troll King lives. Preposterous, he says.
gossip: The Ice Troll King is dead. Burowgar has the head to prove it.
Neitiznot's bridges are fixed and they're mining runite again.
Beard tax on Jatizso now. A beard tax!
Yak meat's still banned on Jatizso. Orders of the King.
starter/compliment: Hail the conquering hero! Anything I can do for you?
