starter/insult: Tax collector, is it? You're not going to tax me, are you?
starter/remark: Ja, it iz so. Ne, it iz not. Every morning. Every morning.

compliment: Veos on the dock has work for a mainlander. You'd suit it.
Veos needs someone to visit all five cities. You look well travelled.
insult: Veos is looking for someone curious. He may lower his standards.
plain/insult: Fresh off the boat and already loitering. Veos will find you a job.
remark: Veos keeps talking about a client from the mainland. Never says who.
gossip: Veos has a client on the mainland asking about Kourend. Who, though?
No king here for twenty years. The Council rules. Such as it is.
Beware the thieves in Piscarilius, Veos tells everyone. Everyone.
starter/compliment: Hello again! My client wants to know about Kourend. Interested?
starter/insult: Hello again! Nothing for you... unless you'd walk to five cities?
starter/remark: A scroll, a quill, a client who sees everything... Best not to ask.

compliment: You're the one who toured all five cities for Veos? Thorough.
Word is you went all the way to the Dark Altar for a stranger. Nerve.
insult: I hear you smashed an orb at the Dark Altar for someone you never met.
plain/insult: Carried a glowing quill round Kourend and burnt your hand. Scholarly.
remark: Veos went very odd for a moment, they say. Not his own voice.
gossip: Veos's client never gave a name. Knowledge can be a curse, he says.
Something was done at the Dark Altar, the Arceuus folk mutter.
Veos says his client's very pleased. Veos doesn't remember saying it.
starter/compliment: Hello again, friend! What can I do for you? Anywhere you'd like to go?
starter/insult: I haven't spoken to you since the boat, you know. Whatever you think.
starter/remark: Knowledge can be a curse... did I say that? I don't recall.

compliment: Tomas Lawry by the bank wants the gangs looked at. You look the part.
The gangs are banding together under some queen. Someone should look.
insult: Tomas Lawry needs someone who looks poor. He'll be thrilled with you.
plain/insult: The Saviours of Kourend recruit from the gutter. Mind how you stand.
remark: A new gang's swallowing the old ones, they say. The Saviours.
gossip: The gangs have a queen now. Nobody's seen her face.
The Saviours of Kourend. Saving us from what, I'd like to know.
Robert O'Reilly would sell his mother for a stew. All we get is fish.
starter/compliment: Greetings. You look poor. Perfect. I've important Council business.
starter/insult: Greetings. Important Council business. You'll do. Barely.
starter/remark: Gangs. A nuisance, but manageable. Until this queen of theirs.

compliment: You're the one who brought down Councillor Hughes? Good riddance.
Word is you got into the Saviours' warren and out again. Bold.
insult: Joined a gang to catch a gang, I hear. Which one are you in now?
plain/insult: Conrad King's dead on the docks, and you were new in town. Hmm.
remark: Lawry's practising an acceptance speech. For a seat he hasn't got.
gossip: Councillor Hughes is in a cell at the castle. Yama cultists, no less!
The gangs' queen was never caught. Funny, that.
Devan Rutter's still about. Business as usual on the docks.
starter/compliment: You've done a great service to Kourend. I'll mention you in my speech.
starter/insult: Yes, yes, very good job. Now be on your way. I've a lot of work to do.
starter/remark: Forget the thieves. Hughes and those vile Disciples of Yama...

compliment: Lord Kandur's son is missing. He'd be glad of a steady pair of hands.
Young Artur's gone off somewhere. Help the Lord find him, friend.
insult: Artur's still missing. Even the kitchen staff have looked harder.
plain/insult: The Lord's son's lost and you're admiring the vines. Priorities.
remark: Elena Hosidius says Artur's meant for greatness. Nearly said king.
gossip: Artur's gone missing. The Lord won't say where, or can't.
Chef Olivia knows more about Artur than she lets on, I'd wager.
Artur was always off in the Arceuus Library. Old books.
starter/compliment: Hello there, friend. My eldest, Artur, is missing. Would you help?
starter/insult: A shame we could not meet in better circumstances. Or better company.
starter/remark: Artur... Start with my family and servants. I've asked them all.

compliment: You're the one who brought Artur home from the caves? Bless you.
Word is you found the old Accord. Lost at sea, they said. Not now.
insult: Hopped some stones and killed a snake, I hear. Hosidius rejoices.
plain/insult: Artur found the chest. You carried it home. Lord Kandur thanked you.
remark: Lord Kandur keeps that old Accord close. Says he's no need of it.
gossip: The Royal Accord of Twill's in Hosidius now. The original, no less.
Artur says it's time for another golden age. Says it quietly.
Words cut deeper than blades, Lord Kandur says. Odd, from a farmer.
starter/compliment: Artur is home safe. I hear we have you to thank for that, friend.
starter/insult: I assume you're after what I promised you. Here. Until next time.
starter/remark: The Accord is a weapon. I've no need to use it. Not yet.

compliment: Mori's lost her friend. The Council won't help. Perhaps you will.
Someone in Arceuus has died. Died! You look like you'd ask why.
insult: Someone's died in Arceuus. Not that you'd know what that means here.
plain/insult: The Council did nothing for Mori. You're keeping pace with them.
remark: The people of Arceuus don't get ill. That's what we always said.
gossip: A woman called Thana has died. In Arceuus. It's not possible.
Mori went to the Council about it. They sent her away, of course.
The Dark Altar's power flickered, they whisper. Nobody says it aloud.
starter/compliment: You'd help? Thank you, friend. The Council wouldn't even listen.
starter/insult: The Council never do anything for the people. Nor do most, it seems.
starter/remark: She's... she's dead... Thana... We don't die. We don't.

compliment: You're the one who saved Arceuus from... whatever that was. Thank you.
Word is you went to the Tasakaal under Mount Karuulm. Few dare.
insult: Smashed a strange device by the altar, I hear. Was it the right one?
plain/insult: You saved the immortals. Try saving someone who needed it.
remark: Lord Arceuus is out of his trance, they say. Quieter than before.
gossip: Someone sabotaged the Dark Altar. Deliberately. Who'd dare?
Lord Arceuus took immortality for his dying wife, the Tasakaal say.
Mori goes up to the church to think about Thana. Leave her be.
starter/compliment: Hello there. Thank you for helping us. A good friend to Arceuus.
starter/insult: Hello. I come here to think. Quietly. That was a hint, friend.
starter/remark: It's my way of remembering Thana. A quiet place to think.

compliment: The Assembly's after someone handy. The Doors of Dinh are failing.
Councillor Unkar needs the Doors seen to. You look handy.
insult: The Doors of Dinh are failing. You're on the wrong side of them.
plain/insult: Lady Vulcana wants you gone and a sherry brought. In that order.
remark: Lady Vulcana's on her third sherry. It's not yet noon.
gossip: The Doors of Dinh have a hole in them. The Wintertodt's noticed.
Lady Vulcana doesn't like urgency. She said so. At length.
Undor at the camp says only Dinh's own hammer can mend those Doors.
starter/compliment: Oh, a human. Councillor Unkar has a job for you. I need a sherry.
starter/insult: Who is this human? Why is the human still here? Jorra! Sherry.
starter/remark: Urgency. I don't like urgency. This is quite simply not on.

compliment: So you're the one Undor keeps going on about. The hammer, was it?
Undor says the Doors can be mended now. Thanks to a human, no less.
dwarf/compliment: Dinh's own hammer, back in a dwarf's hand. By Guthix, that's proper.
insult: Poured water between jugs for an hour, I hear. Thirsty work.
plain/insult: Found a hammer in a tower, I hear. Undor did the actual mending.
remark: The Wintertodt grew strong while those Doors were cracked, they say.
gossip: Dinh's own hammer, out of that tower after all these years. Fancy.
Someone made that hole in the Doors on purpose, Undor reckons.
Lady Vulcana celebrated the Doors with a sherry. Then another.
starter/compliment: Oh look, it's the human. Hello, human. Wonderful stuff, the hammer.
starter/insult: Oh. The human is still here. Councillor, why is the human still here?
starter/remark: My plans? Hmm, let me see now... Ah, I know. I'll have a sherry.

compliment: Old Phileas has a mystery about his ancestor. He'd love a visitor.
Phileas Rimor got a parcel with no name on it. He could use a hand.
insult: Phileas wants help with a thousand-year-old mystery. No rush, then.
plain/insult: Nobody digs on Quidamortem without Lord Shayzien's say. Ask nicely.
remark: Magnus Rimor led the King's expedition and never came back, they say.
gossip: A journal turned up at Phileas's door. No name on it. No sender.
King Shayzien the Seventh sent men up Quidamortem, the old story goes.
Phileas was a soldier once. Now he talks to anyone who'll stop.
starter/compliment: Hello there! Not often I get visitors. You know, there's something...
starter/insult: Hello there. Visitors! Well, a visitor. Don't rush off like the last.
starter/remark: Magnus Rimor... the mountain... a parcel with no name. Curious.

compliment: You roped down into a cave under Quidamortem? I'd not trust the rope.
Word is you brought back proof from the mountain. Lizards and all.
insult: Killed a lizard in a cave and called it history, I hear.
plain/insult: Phileas is gone and his house is wrecked. You were the last to call.
remark: Phileas's house was turned over. Nobody's seen him since.
gossip: Phileas Rimor's gone missing. Lord Shayzien's men are asking about.
Lizards on the mountain. Do not trust the King. So said the bones.
Lord Shayzien wants anything from the mountain brought to him first.

compliment: Cook's cooking for someone very important tonight. He could use help.
Cook needs odd things fetched for a feast. You've a nose for odd.
insult: Cook's still short of a rotten tomato. It's not a hard thing to find.
plain/insult: Cook wants a Dirty Blast. No, I don't know either. Ask him, not me.
remark: Cook's got an ancient cookbook out. Dust everywhere.
gossip: An important meeting at the castle tonight, they whisper. Hush-hush.
Cook's ancestor cooked a feast here a hundred years ago, he says.
Cook's after greenman's ale now. Castle Wars drink, that.
starter/compliment: My friend! I'm in a terrible pickle and need someone trustworthy. You!
starter/insult: It's a very important meeting. Do try to hurry. For once.
starter/remark: Franizzard Van Lumbcook... a job for life... and here I am, a failure.

compliment: King Arthur's after a worthy sort to help free Merlin. You'd do.
insult: Merlin's been stuck in that crystal for ages. No hurry, clearly.
plain/insult: The knights can't free Merlin. I'd not fancy your chances either.
remark: They moved Merlin up to his tower. Crystal and all.
gossip: Merlin's got himself trapped in a crystal, they say. A wizard!
Some say a witch put Merlin in that crystal. The knights won't say.
starter/compliment: Welcome to my court! Seek knighthood? Then help me free Merlin.
starter/insult: Lancelot doubts a commoner could free Merlin. Do prove him wrong.
starter/remark: Merlin, trapped in a crystal. And he was the clever one.
kid/remark: Is the wizard really stuck in a crystal? Can I see? Please?

compliment: Word is you freed Merlin. Camelot's grateful, traveller.
An honorary knight of the Round Table! Fair play to you.
insult: Merlin's free, I hear. Shame about the crystal. Made a nice lamp.
plain/insult: Honorary knight, is it? The honorary bit's doing a lot of work.
gossip: They say Excalibur itself shattered Merlin's crystal.
The Lady of the Lake gave Excalibur away, they say. For bread.
starter/compliment: Ah, my good knight! Camelot owes you a great deal.
starter/insult: Lancelot still says it was luck. I'm sure it wasn't. Mostly.
rough/compliment: Ye got Merlin out of that crystal? Blimey. Good on ye.
kid/compliment: Are you a real knight now? Have you got a sword? Show me!

compliment: Arthur's sending his knights after the Holy Grail. You're a knight.
insult: None of Arthur's knights found the Grail last time. No pressure.
remark: Merlin's set up by the library now. Ask him about the Grail.
gossip: The Grail's passed into Gielinor, they say. Arthur's thrilled.
Young Percival rode off months back and isn't home yet, they say.
starter/compliment: Aha! I'm glad you're here. I'm sending knights after the Grail!
starter/insult: The Grail is very elusive. Perseverance, my knight. A great deal.
starter/remark: Percival's still not back. We are getting a bit worried.
kid/remark: The Grail's a cup, isn't it? All this fuss over a cup?

compliment: Word is you brought the Holy Grail back to Camelot. Splendid!
They say the Fisher King's lands grow green again. Your doing.
insult: Found the Grail, I hear. The knights had only been looking for years.
plain/insult: Found a knight in a goblin sack, I hear. Check your sacks, lads.
gossip: Sir Percival's a king now, they say. Of somewhere nobody can find.
They found Percival in a goblin sack. Three months a slave!
starter/compliment: My splendid knight! Camelot is in your debt.
starter/insult: Ah, the Grail-finder. My other knights are rather sulky about it.
vicar/compliment: The Holy Grail, found! Saradomin smile on you, friend.
kid/compliment: You found the magic cup! Can I drink out of it? Please?

compliment: Old Dimintheis wants his family crest back. A noble cause, that.
insult: The Fitzharmon crest is still lost. Not that you've looked.
remark: That nobleman by the fancy dress shop's lost his estate, I hear.
gossip: Dimintheis's sons went off with the crest. Not seen since.
One of the Fitzharmon boys cooks now, they say. Past the mountain.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! I desperately need my family crest returned to me.
starter/insult: Gah! If you're begging, go and get a job. If not, my crest!
starter/remark: The King has my estate until I show my crest. Wretched rule.
toff/remark: Lost his crest, has Dimintheis. Careless, for a Fitzharmon.
guard/remark: Nobleman by the gate keeps asking after his sons. Not my job.

compliment: Word is you put the Fitzharmon crest back together. Clever work.
You're the one who found all three Fitzharmon boys? Well done.
insult: I hear you cooked fish for a chef to win a crest. Heroic.
plain/insult: Mended a family crest, I hear. Shame you can't mend a family.
gossip: One Fitzharmon son lost his bit of the crest to a demon, they say.
Dimintheis has his crest back, they say. Ever so pleased, he is.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Words are insufficient for the gratitude I feel.
starter/insult: Lost those gauntlets again? Never mind. They always come back.
kid/remark: You fought a demon for a bit of a badge? Grown-ups are odd.

compliment: Caroline's not heard from her husband all week. Help her, would you?
insult: Caroline's family's still out on that platform. You're still here.
remark: No word from the fishing platform for days. Odd, that.
gossip: None of the platform fishermen have written home. Families fret.
Holgart's boat is full of holes, they say. Wants swamp paste.
starter/compliment: Is there any chance you could help me? It's my husband and son.
starter/insult: Kent always writes. Always. You don't look much of a sailor, mind.
starter/remark: Kent and Kennith... not a word all week. It's very strange.
rough/remark: Platform lads have gone quiet. Sea's not right, I tell ye.

compliment: Word is you got young Kennith off that platform. Brave, that.
You're the one who found Kent washed up on that island?
insult: I hear a slug nearly got the better of you. A slug.
gossip: Slugs got into the platform fishermen's heads, they say. Slugs!
Kent's home resting, they say. Won't be fishing for a while.
starter/compliment: Brave adventurer! I could have lost them both but for you.
starter/insult: Kent's home under my feet all day now. Thank you. I think.
rough/insult: Sea slugs, was it? I'd have sorted it with a boot, me.
kid/remark: Did the slugs make the fishermen go funny? Are they slimy?

compliment: Those dwarves by the mountain want a fishing trophy. You fish?
insult: The dwarves still won't let anyone through. Can't say I blame them.
remark: Dwarves guarding a tunnel and talking about fishing. Odd lot.
gossip: The Hemenster contest's on again. Old Jack won it years running.
A pale stranger fishes at Hemenster. Can't abide garlic, they say.
starter/compliment: Friends, is it? Then win us the Hemenster trophy. It's gold!
starter/insult: You can't go down there. Because you can't. So that's fine.
starter/remark: First prize is gold. We dwarves are big fans of gold.

compliment: Word is you won the Hemenster contest. Biggest carp in years!
insult: Won the fishing contest, I hear. With garlic. In a pipe.
plain/insult: Beat a stranger at fishing by stinking out his spot. Champion.
gossip: The dwarves let a stranger through their tunnel. Unheard of!
The stranger in black lost his spot by the pipes, they say. Garlic.
starter/compliment: Ah, our friend! Come on through. Stop in for a beer or two.
starter/insult: Still can't believe a human out-fished us. Mind, we can't fish.
dwarf/compliment: The brothers let you through the tunnel? You must be all right.

remark: There's an odd crack in the wall of that smithy. Always has been.
plain/insult: Rummaging in other folks' bookcases again? Adventurers.
gossip: There's an old book on a magic ore in a house by the bank, they say.
Old tales say wizards sealed a workshop round here. Scared of it.
kid/remark: Mum says there's a secret room under the smithy. I can't find it.

compliment: Word is you got the old workshop running again. Clever hands.
insult: Banging under the smithy all hours, I hear. That was you, then?
remark: Elementals stomping about under the smithy, they say. Lovely.
gossip: A shield of some strange ore, they say. Made right under our feet!
kid/compliment: Did you fight a rock monster? A real one? Down there?

remark: Someone's had all the helpful books off the earth sciences shelf.
plain/insult: Another adventurer in the library. Do put the books back.
gossip: The scholars here found more on that odd elemental ore, they say.
There's a beaten old book in the library. Written in some code.

compliment: Word is you made a helmet from that odd ore. For the mind, no less.
You cracked the code in that old book? The scholars are impressed.
plain/insult: A helmet that sharpens the mind, I hear. Did it work? Hard to say.
gossip: There's a whole lower level under that old workshop, they say.

compliment: Lord Sinclair's been murdered! The guards could use a sharp mind.
insult: Still no culprit for poor Lord Sinclair. Fancy a look, do you?
plain/insult: The guards are baffled by the Sinclair murder. So are you, I'd say.
remark: Study door locked from the inside, they say. And an odd smell.
gossip: Old Lord Sinclair, stabbed in his own study. Terrible business.
Sinclair gave his castle to those knights. His children were furious.
starter/compliment: Oh, it's terrible! Lord Sinclair's been murdered. Can you help?
starter/insult: This is private property! Unless you'd like questioning yourself?
starter/remark: The Sarge says every murder leaves clues. We're out of our depth.

compliment: Word is you solved the Sinclair murder. Fingerprints and all!
insult: Dusting cups with flour, I hear. Is that detective work now?
plain/insult: Apparently you aren't as stupid as you look. Or so they say.
gossip: One of the Sinclairs is under house arrest, awaiting trial.
The guards admit they'd never have solved it alone. Honest of them.
starter/compliment: Excellent work on that murder! All the guards are impressed.
starter/insult: No, your work here is done. Really. Done. You can go.

compliment: Sir Ceril's had cultists in his house. He'd pay for help, I hear.
insult: Sir Ceril's armour's still missing. Wouldn't fit you anyway.
remark: Cultists in a cave south of the city, they say. By the clock tower.
gossip: Cultists broke into the Carnillean house five times. Took one thing!
The Carnilleans' old butler followed the cult once. Died next night.
starter/compliment: You there! Get my stolen armour back and I'll pay you. Modestly.
starter/insult: That's Sir Ceril to you, you impudent scamp. Now, my armour!
starter/remark: Blooming, thieving cultists! String them all up, I say!
toff/remark: The Carnilleans and their cultists. Some families invite trouble.

compliment: Word is you went down among those cultists and came back. Brave.
insult: Turned valves in the sewers all day, I hear. Fragrant work.
remark: Something went on at the Carnillean house. Nobody's saying what.
gossip: The Carnilleans' cult trouble's gone quiet. Quiet isn't over.
starter/compliment: Hello again, adventurer! Do mind the cultists out there.
starter/insult: That's Sir Ceril to you. Still. Good day, I suppose.
starter/remark: Cultists in the sewers, cultists at the door. Blooming cultists!

compliment: Brother Kojo's clock has stopped. He'd pay someone to fix it.
insult: Still no clock. I've been late for everything. Thanks ever so.
remark: Does anyone know the time? That clock tower's no use at all.
gossip: Kojo says the cogs are down in the cellar. With strange beasts.
starter/compliment: Hello, adventurer! Do you happen to know the time? Nor do I!
starter/insult: The cogs are too heavy for me. You look... well, you'll manage.
starter/remark: One cog on each floor... but which goes where? Oh dear.
kid/remark: The big clock's broken. So I can stay up as long as I like!

compliment: Word is you fixed the clock tower. We all know the time again!
insult: You fixed the clock, I hear. Now I've no excuse for being late.
plain/insult: Carried some cogs up a tower. The bards will be thrilled.
gossip: Somebody poisoned the rats under the clock tower. Good riddance.
starter/compliment: Well done, well done! You are clever! It keeps perfect time.
starter/insult: Ah, my cog-carrier! The clock's fine, before you ask.
kid/remark: The clock works again. Now I have to go to bed on time.

compliment: Councillor Halgrive needs plague sheep dealt with. Brave work.
insult: Nobody wants to touch those sick sheep. You included, I see.
remark: Some sheep got loose north of the city. Funny colour, they say.
gossip: The mourners say those loose sheep have the plague. They'd know.
starter/compliment: Adventurer! Four diseased sheep must be dealt with. Will you help?
starter/insult: I do not blame you. It is not pleasant work. Still, time is short.
starter/remark: Every second they're loose, the risk of contagion grows!
rough/remark: Plague in sheep? Never heard the like. Mind, I'm no mourner.

compliment: Word is you rounded up those plague sheep. Brave, in that suit.
insult: I hear you chased sheep about with a cattle prod. Very heroic.
plain/insult: Herded sheep in a plague suit. You'd fit in with the mourners.
gossip: Those sick sheep went in the incinerator, they say. Every one.
starter/compliment: Ah, adventurer! Public health thanks you. As do I.
starter/insult: You've washed since, I trust? One can't be too careful.
kid/remark: You chased coloured sheep with a stick? Can I have a go?

compliment: The Watchtower wizards need help. Ogres about, they say.
insult: The Watchtower's broken and ogres are coming. Don't rush, though.
remark: More ogres in the Feldip Hills lately. The wizards are fretting.
gossip: The tower's power crystals have gone, they say. Stolen!
starter/compliment: Help? Oh, wonderful, dear traveller! Search the bushes for clues!
starter/insult: Typical, nowadays. It's left to us wizards to do all the work.
starter/remark: Oh dear, oh dear. Darn and drat! The crystals!
guard/remark: Ogres at the walls and the tower's broken. Lovely shift, this.

compliment: Word is you got the Watchtower working. Yanille's safe at last!
They say you walked right into Gu'Tanoth. Among the ogres!
insult: Fixed the Watchtower, I hear. The ogres send their regards.
plain/insult: Made friends with ogres, I hear. That explains the smell.
gossip: The ogres' little grey servants pinched the crystals, they say.
starter/compliment: Greetings, friend! Yanille is safe at last, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Ho, ho! A comedian to the finish. Still here, are you?
guard/remark: The tower's shield is up. Fewer ogres, more paperwork.

compliment: Bert the sandman found something nasty in his pit. Ask him.
insult: Bert's still in a state over that sand pit. You walked right past.
remark: Bert's hauling sand all hours lately. Never used to.
gossip: They found a hand in the sand pit, they say. Just a hand!
The guard captain's in the Dragon Inn again. He never leaves it.
starter/compliment: Will you lend us a hand? Ah. Sorry. Poor choice o' words.
starter/insult: Tha guard captain's no help. Doubt you'll be much better.
starter/remark: Wha' shall I do? I'll most certainly lose the job...
guard/remark: A hand in the sand pit. The captain says it's not his department.

compliment: Word is you caught Sandy out. Truth serum in his coffee, no less!
insult: I hear you went round collecting body parts. Hands-on work.
plain/insult: Carried a wizard's head about in your bag, I hear. Charming.
gossip: The sand pit fills itself now, they say. The wizards saw to it.
Sandy's wanted by the guards. Bribed a wizard, then did him in.
starter/compliment: Ey up! The pit fills itself now. No more work for Bert!
starter/insult: I'd shake yer hand, but I've gone right off hands, see.
barkeep/remark: The guard captain's still on about some hand. Drank through it.

compliment: Brother Omad's not slept in a week. A child's blanket was stolen.
insult: Thieves took a baby's blanket. And still nobody's fetched it.
remark: There's a ring of stones in the forest west of here. Odd, that.
gossip: Brother Cedric went off for wine days ago. Not back, they say.
starter/compliment: Oh, hello... sorry, so tired. Could you find the child's blanket?
starter/insult: We are peaceful men. You look... less so. Good. The blanket!
starter/remark: Waaaah! Waaaah! All night long! I need some sleep!
vicar/remark: Brother Omad's yawning through prayers again. Poor soul.

compliment: Word is you got the monks their party. And their wine!
insult: Found a baby's blanket and a drunk monk, I hear. Busy day.
gossip: Brother Cedric's back with the wine, they say. Mostly sober.
The monastery threw a birthday party. Monks! Partying!
starter/compliment: Ah, my friend! Much better now I'm sleeping. Fancy a party?
starter/insult: Hello, adventurer. Do keep it down. The little one's asleep.
vicar/compliment: You helped the brothers at the monastery? Saradomin smile on you.

compliment: The professor at the Observatory needs help. Goblins wrecked it.
insult: The professor's telescope's still broken. The stars can wait, then.
remark: Goblins moved in by the Observatory. Nothing but trouble since.
gossip: The assistant says that telescope hasn't worked in ages.
starter/compliment: Welcome to the Observatory, where wonder is all around you!
starter/insult: Don't listen to my assistant. Or do. You'll help either way?
starter/remark: Those pesky goblins tampered with my telescope. Pesky!

compliment: Word is you got the Observatory telescope working. Splendid!
insult: You looked at the stars, I hear. I do that for free most nights.
gossip: The assistant says you made the lens yourself. Wise, that.
The Observatory goblins made stew in the lens mould, they say.
starter/compliment: My friend! The heavens are ours again, thanks to you!
starter/insult: You again? Don't touch anything. My assistant's orders.
kid/remark: Did you see a star? Can you get me one? A little one?

compliment: Kangai Mau wants someone sneaky for a job in Ardougne. You?
insult: Kangai Mau wants a skilled thief. Keep walking, then.
remark: Some Ardougne lord took a totem from the Rantuki tribe, they say.
gossip: Lord Handelmort collects things. Other people's things, mostly.
starter/compliment: Hello. I Kangai Mau of Rantuki tribe. You look brave and sneaky.
starter/insult: I told I find thieves in Brimhaven. Not you, maybe.
starter/remark: Handelmort think he have right to take our totem. He wrong.
barkeep/remark: That tribesman's had a table all week, waiting on a thief.

compliment: Word is you got the Rantuki totem back from that Ardougne lord.
insult: Burgled a lord's private museum, I hear. For swordfish.
gossip: They say someone got into Handelmort's house by teleport.
starter/compliment: You! Totem home now. Rantuki tribe grateful. Have swordfish.
starter/insult: You again. I hope you not steal from me now.
pirate/compliment: Burgled a lord for a tribesman, did ye? Arr, I like that.

compliment: Lady Servil's family was taken by Khazard's men. Help her.
insult: Lady Servil's still waiting by her broken cart. Still.
remark: Khazard's mercenaries run this whole area. Nobody stops them.
gossip: Khazard's men make folk fight in that arena. For sport!
They say the authorities take Khazard's coin and look away.
starter/compliment: Adventurer, please... bring back my family. They're in the arena.
starter/insult: The cart? That's the least of my problems! Unless you can fight?
starter/remark: Justin... Sammy... I've got to find my family.

compliment: Word is you freed the Servils from Khazard's arena. Bravo!
You're the one who killed Khazard's hellhound? Blimey.
plain/insult: Fought in Khazard's arena, I hear. Did you take a bow after?
gossip: Khazard's still raging over his dog, they say. Bouncer, it was.
The Servils are home and recovering, they say. Good news.
starter/compliment: My husband and son are safe at home, thanks to you!
starter/insult: Do mind Khazard's men. They hold grudges, you know.
kid/remark: You beat a hellhound? Was it big? Did it have spikes?

compliment: Otto by the falls teaches the old barbarian ways. You'd suit it.
insult: Otto says you've barbarian blood. He's very generous, Otto.
remark: Otto fishes without a harpoon, they say. Sharks and all.
gossip: Otto talks with the spirits of the dead, they say. Barbarian ones.
starter/compliment: Good day! You seem a hearty warrior. Barbarian blood, perhaps?
starter/insult: Your scepticism will be your loss, civilised one.
starter/remark: May the spirits be with you. And with your arm, near sharks.

compliment: Word is Otto's taught you the old ways. Fire without a tinderbox!
insult: Catch fish with your bare arm now, I hear. Hard on the sleeves.
plain/insult: Plant saplings with your fist now, I hear. A gardener's nightmare.
gossip: There's a cavern under Otto's lake, they say. Full of dragons.
starter/compliment: Good day, hearty warrior! The ancestors are proud of you.
starter/insult: You still hold back too much. Spoken as a friend, mind.
kid/compliment: Can you really catch a fish with just your hands? Teach me!

compliment: Only the elite get into the Legends' Guild. You might, you know.
insult: They don't call it the Legends' Guild for nothing, you know.
remark: The guild wants the Kharazi Jungle mapped. Nobody's managed it.
gossip: The south of Karamja's never been mapped, they say. Too thick.
starter/compliment: Good day, adventurer! No doubt you're keen to join the guild?
starter/insult: You'll need to be a legendary citizen. Best of luck with that.
starter/remark: Grand Vizier Erkle is a very busy man. Do be brief.

compliment: Word is you mapped the Kharazi Jungle. A true legend, then.
That totem in the main hall? They say you brought it back.
insult: Mapped a jungle, I hear. Did you get lost? Just a bit?
plain/insult: A member of the Legends' Guild. They're letting anyone in now.
gossip: They say a demon had hold of a Kharazi shaman. Not any more.
The Kharazi tribe call the guild friends now, they say.
starter/compliment: Welcome, legend. Your totem has pride of place in the hall.
starter/insult: Ah, our newest legend. Do wipe the jungle off your boots.

compliment: A stranger at the Flying Horse wants a hero. Pays well, he says.
insult: The limping stranger's still looking for a hero. Still looking.
remark: Fellow in the Flying Horse walks with a limp. Gives me the chills.
gossip: He's after something in the old Temple of Ikov, they say.
starter/compliment: I seek a hero to go on an important mission! Are you one?
starter/insult: Call yourself a hero? My daughter is more of a hero than you!
starter/remark: My patience grows thin. The Staff of Armadyl, hero!
barkeep/remark: That limping one wants a hero. I just want him to order something.

compliment: Word is you went into the Temple of Ikov and came back out.
You got past the fire warrior in Ikov? With ice arrows? Clever.
insult: That limping stranger hasn't been back. Did you scare him off?
gossip: That limping stranger was Lucien, some say. A Mahjarrat!
kid/remark: Was the temple full of spiders? Ice ones? Did they bite?

compliment: The Hunter Guild could use a sharp-eyed tracker. Ask the Guildmaster.
plain/insult: The guild wants trackers. You'd lose your own footprints.
remark: Hunters come and go from this guild. Some just go, mind.
gossip: Fox left the guild without a word to anyone. Verity's fretting.
Wolf sent Fox off on some errand, they say. Nobody's seen him since.
kid/remark: The guild cat's called a hunter. He just sleeps all day!
starter/compliment: A little birdy tells me Verity could use a hand, hunter.
starter/insult: Can't find the Burrow? Then maybe you're not cut out for this guild.
starter/remark: Politics and paperwork. I was a hunter once, you know.

compliment: You found Fox out on the savannah and patched him up, I hear.
The guild gives you the hard rumours now, they say. That's trust.
insult: Mended a cat's bed for the Hunter Guild, I hear. The bards are told.
plain/insult: You tracked down Fox. He was lying flat. Not hard to catch, then.
gossip: Something knocked Fox out cold on the savannah. He never saw what.
Kiko's got a proper fur bed again. The whole guild can relax.
kid/compliment: You found Fox! I thought he'd be a real fox. He's just a man.
starter/compliment: Nilsal, hunter. Fox is back on his feet, thanks to you.
starter/insult: Don't let it go to your head, hunter. Kiko did most of the work.

compliment: Marcellus needs someone calm to talk to the frogs. You'd do.
plain/insult: Frogs on strike, and you're the best the oasis could find?
remark: Don't mention frogs near Marcellus. He's had a trying time.
gossip: The frogs at the oasis have gone on strike, they say. Frogs!
Marcellus reckons the frogs want to enslave us all. Keeps saying it.
kid/remark: The frogs are on strike! Can I go on strike too?
starter/compliment: You're no frog, are you? Good. I need someone I can trust.
starter/insult: You! I bet you're with them! The frogs!
starter/remark: They're out to get us. All of us. Frogs, I tell you!

compliment: You made peace between Marcellus and the frogs? Remarkable.
The oasis frogs are back eating the flies, thanks to you, I hear.
insult: I hear you settled a dispute between a farmer and some frogs. Grand.
plain/insult: Brokered peace with frogs. They'll be carving your statue, no doubt.
gossip: The frogs held an election, they say. Hopping on lily pads.
Marcellus pays the frogs in oranges now. Strange times.
There's a frog calling himself Lord of Dread. Nobody's worried.
kid/insult: You fought a frog? Was it a big frog? It was a small one, wasn't it.
starter/compliment: Hello again. My patch is yours, friend. The flies won't win.
starter/insult: Back again? Keep your voice down. The flies are listening.

compliment: The villa's after smart staff for the party. You'd scrub up well.
plain/insult: A fancy party at the villa. They'd make you use the back door.
remark: That actor by the villa gate is still waiting for his big break.
gossip: A party at Villa Lucens tonight, they say. Aldarin's finest, invited.
There's a new play opening at the villa's theatre, up on the cliffs.
starter/compliment: Good day! Could I trouble you for the briefest of moments?
starter/insult: On second thoughts, you may not be cut out for this job.
starter/remark: Patzi the Grand, they'll call me. Eventually.

compliment: You're the one who solved the death at Villa Lucens? Well done.
Accused of murder and cleared your own name, I hear. Sharp work.
insult: Accused the bag carrier first, I hear. Well, she was a thief.
plain/insult: Stole the show at the villa, they say. With a prop sword.
gossip: The show went on at Villa Lucens, death or no. The host insisted.
One of the cast tripped him, they say. Too much wine, and a long fall.
Somebody was after the Principum Red in the villa cellar, I hear.
toff/compliment: A butler who solves murders. Constantinius should hire more.
starter/compliment: Ah, my butler! I'll be a star yet, you mark my words.
starter/insult: You upstaged me! I hired you to make me look better!

compliment: Emelio's after an easterner for some venture. That's you, friend.
plain/insult: Emelio needs an easterner's help. He'll take you, apparently.
remark: Emelio was Varlaless once, you know. Couldn't abide outsiders.
gossip: Emelio's got a new business idea. Something from the east.
The Colosseum's still cleaning up after Emelio's last idea, I hear.
starter/compliment: You're one of them easterners, aren't you? Kuani! I need you!
starter/insult: You don't know the kabit? But how could you not know?
starter/remark: Meat, spices and salad, all wrapped in bread. Genius!

compliment: Kebabs in Varlamore! You had a hand in that, they say.
You ate a kebab and fought a minotaur in the Colosseum? Showman.
insult: Fought a minotaur for an advert, I hear. Glamorous work.
plain/insult: A minotaur fight to sell kebabs. I hope they paid you well.
gossip: Emelio's opened a kebab shop. Buffalo, with Kharidian spice.
The minotaur thought you'd eaten minotaur meat. It was buffalo.
kid/compliment: You're the kebab one! Can I have a kebab? Please?
starter/compliment: Nilsal, friend! A special price for you, as always.
starter/insult: Sorry, friend, the next customers come first. Even before you.

compliment: The curator could use a sharp pair of eyes at the museum.
plain/insult: The curator wants a detective. He's got you instead.
remark: An empty case at the museum. Folk queue up to look at nothing.
gossip: Xerna's Diadem was stolen from the Grand Museum. Right off display!
The guards are looking into the museum theft. Slowly, I hear.
guard/remark: Museum theft is under investigation. Move along.
starter/compliment: Perhaps you'd have better luck finding it than the guards.
starter/insult: I'm no detective. Forgive me, but I'm not sure you are either.
starter/remark: Xerna's Diadem, gone. And nothing else even out of place.

compliment: Xerna's Diadem is back at the museum. You found it, I hear.
You followed the diadem's trail across the sea, they say. Well done.
insult: Found the diadem, I hear. Won't say where. Very mysterious.
plain/insult: Found the diadem and kept quiet where. Smells fishy, friend.
gossip: The diadem's back on display. Where it went, nobody's saying.
A grey-haired man with a monocle was asking about boats, they say.
guard/remark: Diadem's back. Case closed. Don't ask me how.
starter/compliment: Thank you again, iknami. The diadem has never looked finer.
starter/insult: One day you'll tell me where you found it. I am a patient man.

compliment: Folk keep vanishing round here. We could use someone brave.
plain/insult: Folk vanishing, and you're after a pint? Read the board, friend.
remark: Some say the missing got lost in the mountains. Others say Fortis.
Francis swears the ents walked a different path that night.
gossip: More missing folk on the board at the pub. It's never ending.
Old Ictus says the night people took them. Nobody listens to him.
starter/compliment: Please. If you truly care, help us find our sons.
starter/insult: Turn around. Walk out. Nobody's looking into anything.
starter/remark: One moment they were playing upstairs. The next, gone.

compliment: You brought Shas and Etz home? Their parents can sleep again.
You went into that den and brought Antos out alive. Brave.
insult: Ictus says he told you so. Mind, he tells everyone so.
plain/insult: Turns out the madman by the sea was right. You took your time.
gossip: Ictus was right all along. Something did come in the night.
Not everyone came back from that cave. Only the boys and Antos.
The captain's guards have new bows at last. Willow, I hear.
kid/remark: Shas says there were monsters in the cave. Real ones!
starter/compliment: Our boys are home because of you. We'll never forget it.
starter/insult: You again? Oh. It's you. Come in, then. Mind the new wall.

compliment: That tourist at the temple wants a guest. Kind of you to visit.
plain/insult: A man and his egg, up at the temple. You'd get on.
remark: Somebody ought to tell that tourist the temple isn't a house.
gossip: There's a tourist living in Tal Teok temple. With an egg.
That tourist talks to his egg. Calls it his best friend.
kid/remark: There's an egg sat on the temple wall! The man talks to it!
starter/compliment: You found me! Do stay for a feast. Humpy Plumpy insists.
starter/insult: Could I trust you with Humpy Plumpy? He's very delicate.
starter/remark: I've come to quite like it here. Best friend I ever had, this egg.

compliment: You put that egg back together, piece by piece? That's patience.
insult: Lost one egg and broke three more, I hear. Steady hands.
plain/insult: Chicken egg, dragon egg, jaguar egg, all smashed. Thorough work.
remark: Gravity's been very busy up at the temple, they say.
gossip: That tourist up at Tal Teok had a great fall, they say. Poor Alan.
King lent all her men out to mend an egg. I am not making this up.
barkeep/remark: King's men, sent up the hill for an egg. Strangest order going.
kid/compliment: You fixed the egg! Can you fix mine? I dropped it.

compliment: That scholar could use help with the ents. You've a kind face.
plain/insult: The funny man's after help with the ents. You'll fit right in.
remark: Ents, totems, spirits. All one cycle out here, the old folk say.
gossip: That scholar keeps staring at the ents. Lost in thought, always.
Somebody's been asking what the totems are for. Out-of-towner.
kid/remark: The funny man gets confused by the ents! I've been watching him!
starter/compliment: Oh! You gave me quite the start. Do you know anything of ents?
starter/insult: The locals told me nothing useful. I doubt you'll do better.
starter/remark: These totems matter to the ents. But why? I need more notes.

compliment: You rebuilt a totem for the ents? They'll remember that.
The ents left you an offering, I hear. That's an honour.
insult: Watched the scholar break a totem, then fixed it. Tidy, that.
plain/insult: Carving animals on a pole to cheer up trees. Proud day for you.
gossip: A little girl showed that scholar how to carve a totem, they say.
The ents are happy again. The totem's back up, carvings and all.
kid/compliment: You fixed the totem! The ents aren't sad any more!
starter/compliment: Ah, my fellow ent watcher! The totems are doing splendidly.
starter/insult: You again? I've written you into my notes. As a footnote.

compliment: Those salvagers on the dock want a captain. Fancy the sea?
plain/insult: Those two want a captain. They'll take anyone. Even you.
remark: Salvage work, they call it. Fishing up old wrecks for coin.
gossip: Two salvagers on the dock, hiring. Very keen. Too keen, I'd say.
Will and Anne are starting a salvage business. Looking for hands.
starter/compliment: Ah, look what we have here! Someone who needs a good job!
starter/insult: This one's clearly never worked an honest day in their life!
starter/remark: You waive all rights in the event of horrific death? Splendid!

compliment: Washed up on the Pandemonium and came back a sailor. Fair play.
insult: Got your first job and went straight overboard, I hear.
plain/insult: Thrown overboard on your first day. Most of us last a bit longer.
remark: Boats everywhere these days. Everyone's a sailor now.
gossip: Those salvagers sailed off with some old medallion. Not seen since.
Word is those salvagers shoved their new hand overboard. Charming.
pirate/compliment: Arr, ye've found yer sea legs. The Pandemonium's a fine start.
rough/insult: Floated all the way to the Pandemonium, did ye? Like driftwood.
kid/compliment: You've got a raft! Is it a real boat? Can I steer?

compliment: Steve's after a sailor for some looty. You look the part.
pirate/insult: Steve wants a rough, tough, piratical type. Keep lookin', Steve.
remark: Steve's got a crate behind the bar nobody can get open.
gossip: Steve's on about pirate looty again. In a crate at Port Sarim.
Steve says the looty's disguised as ordinary cargo. Cunning, that.
starter/compliment: Hoist your mast, sailor! There's pirate looty begging to be found!
starter/insult: I'm after a rough, tough, piratical type, and it isn't you!
starter/remark: Precious plundered pirate looty! Nothing normal about it!

compliment: You got Steve's crate open at last. Took a proper sailor.
insult: All that sailing for a crate of crowbars. Worth it, was it?
plain/insult: You needed a crowbar to open a crate of crowbars. Think on that.
gossip: Steve's precious looty was a crate of crowbars. Locked shut.
Someone drank a bottle of old stout and a troll jumped out, they say.
A dwarf near Sarim helped make the key, they say. Paid in pie.
starter/compliment: Yarr! My first mate returns! Still using that raft, are you?
starter/insult: Blistering barnacles! Did I forget to mention the troll?

compliment: Arhein needs a hand with the council. Brave of you to offer.
plain/insult: You, against Councillor Catherine? I'd sell tickets.
remark: Another form from the council office. Catherby runs on forms.
gossip: Arhein's got a bird he swears can read the sea currents.
The councillor's banned non-human workers. Arhein's bird included.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Fancy helping me test a little theory?
starter/insult: You can try Catherine yourself. It'll be an uphill struggle.
starter/remark: A bird that tracks currents. If only the council would let me.

compliment: You beat Councillor Catherine at her own forms? A hero.
You charted the currents for Arhein, I hear. Good work.
insult: Filled in the council's form twice, I hear. Same answers both times.
plain/insult: Fished a mayor out of a tank. Democracy, Catherby style.
gossip: Catherby has a new mayor. Same as the old ones, really. Scales.
Councillor Catherine still hasn't noticed the mayor's a fish.
kid/remark: The mayor's a fish! Everyone knows except the councillor!
starter/compliment: Hello again! Thanks to you, those currents are charted.
starter/insult: Hello again! How's the mayor? Keeping him wet, I hope.

compliment: There's a hurt tortugan on that island. A kind soul might help.
remark: Gryphons have been seen out over the islands. Keep your head down.
gossip: A tortugan's lying hurt out there, they say. Won't let anyone near.
starter/compliment: Bandages... I was trying to make bandages. Seaweed and a leaf...
starter/insult: No... no help. I'll fix it myself...
starter/remark: I'm fine... I'm fine. Please... leave me alone...

compliment: You brought Floopa home. Elder Korel says she'd not have survived.
You saved the Little Pearl from the gryphon. The eggs are safe.
insult: Elder Korel let you stay as a tourist. Don't let it go to your head.
plain/insult: A land walker, mending tortugan roofs. Whatever next?
gossip: A ship with red sails was seen leaving the Little Pearl, they say.
Floopa's wound will never fully heal, Elder Korel says.
Elder Korel can't fathom how a gryphon got out to the Little Pearl.
starter/compliment: Thank you for saving my life. I mean it. I'm just bad at saying so.
starter/insult: I'd have managed. Probably. I read a book once, you know.

compliment: Elder Raley trusts you. Few tourists can say that.
plain/insult: The elders think well of you. I'll wait and see.
remark: That ship with the red sails. Nobody here has forgotten it.
gossip: Elder Raley's looking for Floopa. She should be resting, he says.
Floopa's been seen heading off alone, flipper or no flipper.
starter/compliment: Welcome back. You haven't seen Floopa, have you?
starter/insult: You found Floopa once. Surely you can manage it twice?
starter/remark: She can't have gone far. Not with that flipper.

compliment: You looked into the red-sailed traders for Floopa. That was brave.
The elders gave you the camphor in the Sacred Grove. A rare honour.
insult: You worked for the Red Reef company, I hear. For a while.
plain/insult: Fought pirates for the very traders who hurt Floopa. Neat.
gossip: Spencer Brentwood wants the red coral by the Little Pearl, they say.
Floopa says Spencer stabbed her with her own spear. Then said sorry.
The elders are making plans against the Red Reef company.
starter/compliment: You've been a good friend to us. It means everything.
starter/insult: A plan of our own! Do try to stay out of trouble meanwhile.

compliment: The mayor's asking for help finding Keenan. Brave of you to stay.
plain/insult: Another outsider. We don't need help. Not from your sort.
remark: Outsiders aren't welcome on Wyrmscraig. Most of us mean it.
gossip: Keenan's gone missing. Muriel's in no state for visitors.
The lad was always sat staring at the sunstone in the mine.
starter/compliment: If you're feelin' brave, Keenan's gone missing. Help us look?
starter/insult: Not often we get one like you 'round these parts.
starter/remark: My job is to keep things calm. Not easy, these days.

compliment: You went into Ardeaglais and came back. None of us would have.
You found out what became of Keenan. Hard news, but news.
insult: You're still an outsider, mind. A useful one.
plain/insult: Saved the island from its own angel. Don't expect a statue.
gossip: Keenan's gone. Poor Muriel. At least she knows now.
The Mad Angel's left for good, they say. Left a golem to guard us.
Cormac thought the Angel was just a tale. He knows better now.
starter/compliment: All the best, friend. Good to see you stickin' around.
starter/insult: Still here? Folk might start thinkin' you live on Wyrmscraig.

compliment: Gillie Groats could use help with that bull. You look sturdy.
plain/insult: Cassius wants a partner for his milk scheme. He's not fussy.
remark: Gillie says a bull's been upsetting her cows something rotten.
gossip: There's a bad-tempered bull in the Groats' cow pen. Whose, though?
Some fellow by the pond wants to build an empire. Of milk.
kid/remark: The man by the pond keeps asking people if they like milk!
starter/compliment: You! Yes, you! Do you like making money? And... milk?
starter/insult: Fair enough. If your passion for milk changes, you know where I am.
starter/remark: An empire. Of milk. It's a perfect plan!

compliment: You sorted out that bull for the Groats. Their cows are happy again.
insult: Took on a bull over a jug of milk. Lumbridge's finest hour.
plain/insult: Grabbed a bull by the horns over bad milk. Brave, or daft.
gossip: That bull in the Groats' field was Cassius's, they say. The rogue.
Cassius was stealing milk from the Groats, I hear. Sour stuff it was.
kid/compliment: You beat the big bull! It was bigger than a cow, wasn't it!
starter/insult: You should leave. I can't even look at you.
starter/remark: Ruined it! The unique flavour was what I was trying to sell!

compliment: Talia's shelter needs someone worldly to find strays. You'd do.
plain/insult: Talia wants someone worldly to fetch strays. You'll have to do.
remark: Strays all over, and an empty shelter. Somebody ought to help.
gossip: There's a dog shelter by the monastery. Not many dogs in it yet.
The monks gave Talia and Chase that land. They believe in the cause.
vicar/compliment: Talia's shelter needs a kind soul. Saradomin smile on you.
starter/compliment: Welcome to our dog shelter! We need someone worldly. Like you.
starter/insult: It takes hours to coax a puppy out of hiding. You'd take days.
starter/remark: Kennels to clean, dogs to feed, fences to mend. And no strays.

compliment: You brought puppies home to the shelter? Bless you.
The shelter's open for business now, thanks to you, they say.
insult: Rescued puppies from goblins and outlaws, I hear. Fierce, puppies.
gossip: The goblins wanted puppies for guard dogs. Got a stuffed one instead.
Outlaws had one of the puppies, they say. Not any more.
vicar/compliment: The shelter thrives. Saradomin smile on you, friend.
kid/compliment: You found puppies! Can I have one? I'll call it Biscuit!
starter/compliment: Welcome back! The kennels are full, and it's thanks to you.
starter/insult: Oh, you're here. The kennels need cleaning, since you ask.

gossip: The Professor's got a new assistant up at the manor. Sharp tongue.
The young scientist at the manor can't sleep. Says the bed's vile.
remark: Someone's living behind a bookcase in that manor now. Honestly.
plain/insult: Ava wants undead chickens fetched. You look the gullible sort.
starter/compliment: You there! I need a couple of undead chickens. For science.
starter/insult: You'd fetch anything for a reward, wouldn't you? Good. Chickens.
starter/remark: This bed is vile. And the Professor upstairs is no help at all.

compliment: Word is you helped that scientist build her contraption. Clever.
Ava's made you a gadget that fetches your arrows back, I hear.
insult: Fetched chickens, a magnet and some buttons for a lady. Brave.
plain/insult: Chopped a haunted tree for Ava, I hear. The tree's still sulking.
gossip: Ava's got an undead chicken in her bed now. Science, apparently.
starter/compliment: Ah, my gullible helper. The device works? Of course it does.
starter/insult: Lost your arrows again? I did build you something for that.
kid/remark: Is it true the lady at the manor sleeps on a dead chicken?

gossip: The students up at the dig keep losing things. A teddy, of all things.
You can't dig up there without passing the Earth Sciences exams.
remark: The Varrock museum pays for the dig, they say. Lucky them.
starter/compliment: Hello, dear! Fancy sitting an Earth Sciences exam? They're serious.
starter/insult: An exam? You? Well, get the Curator to stamp your letter first.
starter/remark: Gloves and boots at all times. Why does nobody listen?

compliment: Passed all three exams, they say, then found an altar under it all.
Word is you found a Zarosian altar down the shafts. Fancy that.
gossip: Saradominists buried an old altar under the dig, they reckon.
insult: You blew up a wall down the dig, I hear. For archaeology, apparently.
plain/insult: Carried nitroglycerin round the dig, I hear. In your pack!
starter/compliment: Ah, my star pupil! Still handling bones very carefully, I hope?
starter/insult: Oh, it's you. Every answer wrong the first time, dear. Every one.

gossip: Some folk went to a house party on an island past the swamp.
There's a boat by the fishing spots. Nobody'll say who left it.
remark: Someone was screaming down by the swamp. I didn't go and look.
starter/compliment: Help! Help! We were attacked on the island! Please!
starter/insult: You? Fine. Anyone! Just stop that killer before it's too late.
starter/remark: That psycho is still out there. They can't get away with this.

gossip: That party on the island ended in murder, they say. More than one.
The killer was one of the guests all along, I hear. Shocking.
compliment: You're the one who caught that island killer? Good for you.
plain/insult: Caught the killer, I hear. After how many of the guests, exactly?
remark: Mandy lived through it, they say. Her heart's on the wrong side!
kid/remark: Was there really a murderer in a wardrobe? Did you look in mine?

gossip: A fellow in the Jolly Boar swore he saw zombies marching in ranks.
remark: Zombies don't march, do they? Not in ranks. Surely not.
insult: Zombies forming ranks up north, and here's you sightseeing.
barkeep/remark: Some chap was raving about zombies in here. I cut him off.
starter/compliment: Ah, an adventurer. I could use some help following a trail.
starter/insult: Kind of you to offer. I'd hoped for someone better read, but still.
starter/remark: Zombies forming ranks... someone must be organising them.

compliment: You held the palace when the dead came, they say. Varrock thanks you.
Word is you found the one man who could wake Arrav's shield.
gossip: Zombies at the palace! And Arrav himself leading them, poor soul.
Dimintheis raised the shield and the zombies fell, they say.
insult: Saved the palace, I hear. Shame about the state of the furniture.
plain/insult: The necromancer got away, I hear. Took Arrav with him, too.
toff/compliment: Fitzharmon blood saved the city, they say. One always knew.
guard/remark: Zombies at the palace. Nobody tell me they'll be back.
kid/compliment: Did you see the zombies? Mum made me hide under the bed!

gossip: Arrav's still in that necromancer's grip, they say. Poor soul.
That explorer from the Jolly Boar's gone south to the desert, I hear.
remark: Zemouregal's still out there somewhere. Him and his zombies.

gossip: They say someone stole Arrav's heart back from the necromancer!
compliment: You took Arrav's heart from Zemouregal's own vault? Ye gods.
Word is you faced Arrav himself and walked away. Brave soul.
insult: Robbed a necromancer's vault, I hear. Do mind he doesn't visit.
plain/insult: Got Arrav's heart back, I hear. And Arrav? Still not home, is he?
toff/remark: Arrav, the hero of Avarrocka, kept like a puppet. Disgraceful.
guard/remark: Robbing Mahjarrat now, is it? Don't bring him back here.
kid/remark: You had a real heart in your bag? Was it still beating?

gossip: Outlaws ransacked a trader's cart on this road. Took his papers.
remark: That trader by the crossroads is called Rat. Rat! Poor man.
insult: Rat's still waiting on his papers. Outlaws don't post things back.
starter/compliment: Hello there. I'm Rat. No, Rat's my name. Could you help me?
starter/insult: Look, do you want to help me or not? Those outlaws took my papers!
starter/remark: Five pages. Those outlaws have no idea what they took.

compliment: Rat says you're a credit to... er, to trading. Yes. Trading.
gossip: Funny thing. Nothing at all happened in the palace library. Nothing.
That scholar Surok never leaves the palace library now. Odd, that.
plain/insult: Fought the King, I hear. Don't worry. Nobody believes it.
guard/remark: Nothing happened at the palace. Move along. Nothing at all.
starter/compliment: Ah! You did us a fine service. Er, me. A humble trader.
starter/insult: A bit more muscle and some training, private. Then we'll see.
starter/remark: Things seem pretty quiet. Which is just how we like it.

gossip: The Zamorakians in that chaos temple craft their own runes, I hear.
remark: That mage in the chaos temple sells runes in the Wilderness. Shifty.
starter/compliment: You know of the essence mine? Then perhaps we can do business.
starter/insult: A mercenary with no allegiance. Not my type. Still, you'll do.
starter/remark: Those Saradominist fools in the Order. Inept, the lot of them.

gossip: The Zamorak lot found a way into the wizards' essence mine, I hear.
insult: Helped the wizards, then their rivals. Very even-handed of you.
compliment: You can cross the Abyss now, they say. Rather you than me.
vicar/insult: Helped the Zamorakians, did you? I shall pray for you, friend.
guard/remark: Zamorakians by the rune shop again. I've got my eye on them.
starter/compliment: Ah. Our mercenary. The institute remembers its friends.
starter/insult: Still running errands for the Order of Wizards, I suppose?

gossip: Part of the castle cellar wall fell in. The Duke says earthquake.
Someone swears they saw a goblin with huge eyes in the cellar.
remark: A goblin with a light on its head? In Lumbridge? Never.
barkeep/remark: Rock dust all over my ingredients. Earthquake, my foot.
starter/compliment: Monsters damaged the cellar, I'm sure of it. Ask around, would you?
starter/insult: The Duke says earthquake. You look like you'd believe him.
starter/remark: An earthquake, the Duke says. An earthquake! Monsters, more like.

compliment: You made peace with the goblins under the castle? Well done.
Lumbridge has a treaty with cave goblins now. Your doing, they say.
gossip: Sigmund was a HAM man all along, they say. Who'd have thought?
insult: Did a goblin bow to make friends, I hear. Very dignified.
plain/insult: Peace with goblins, is it? I'll still lock my cellar, thanks.
toff/remark: One has signed a treaty with goblins. Goblins! How times change.
kid/compliment: Are there really goblins under the castle? Can I meet one?

gossip: The Council wants to send one of us up to the surface. Brave.
The Council fears the HAM folk are plotting against us again.
remark: No Dorgeshuun has been up top since the treaty. Is it very bright?
starter/compliment: It is good to see you again! The Council would like a favour.
starter/insult: The Council insists on a surface-dweller to lead. Well. You're here.
starter/remark: We are curious about the surface. And worried about its dangers.

compliment: You stopped them flooding our caves, they say. Thank you.
gossip: HAM wanted to flood the caves with a drilling machine. A machine!
Zanik died on the surface and came back. Her mark glowed, they say.
plain/insult: Took Zanik to see the surface, and she came back dead. Briefly.
starter/compliment: Hello again! The Council has not forgotten what you did.
starter/insult: Ah, you. Next time, perhaps keep our agent alive throughout?

gossip: The dwarves are building a train line from Keldagrim. To here!
Work on the line's stopped. They dug up old goblin things.
dwarf/remark: Our tunnel's held up by goblin relics. Relics! Fetch an expert.
starter/compliment: Do you have any experience with archaeology? We need help.
starter/insult: Hurry the dig, and it's a crime against knowledge. So, slowly.
starter/remark: A train link to Keldagrim. For trade, and for goodwill.

gossip: The train runs to Keldagrim now! Dwarves everywhere.
Sigmund tried to kill Zanik on the tracks, they say. To start a war.
compliment: You stopped a war between us and the dwarves, I hear. Thank you.
insult: Went digging for old pots and came back with a prophecy. Busy day.
dwarf/compliment: The line's open, and no war. By Guthix, that's good work.
starter/compliment: All the Dorgeshuun owe you our lives once again, my friend.
starter/remark: There's quite a craze for surface foods at the market now.

gossip: A surface goblin's at the gate, begging to see Zanik. Again.
Surface goblins aren't allowed in the city. Council's rules.
remark: That little goblin outside keeps on about a dream. Every day.
starter/compliment: You help me get into Dorgesh-city? I want talk to Chosen Commander!
starter/insult: Big human not help Grubfoot either? Nobody ever help Grubfoot.
starter/remark: I have dream. Land of Goblins. Chosen Commander lead us there!

gossip: Zanik vanished in Yu'biusk. Oldak can't get his machine going.
Yu'biusk's a wasteland, they say. Torn apart by the war god himself.
compliment: You walked into the goblin temple dressed as a goblin? Some nerve!
plain/insult: Went all that way for a land of goblins, and lost Zanik there.
remark: Grubfoot says she'll come back one day. Grubfoot's sure of it.
kid/remark: You turned into a goblin? Do it again! Go on!

gossip: There's a wizard sat by the Lumbridge gate. Says she's from the Tower.
That wizard bought an old amulet the smith thought was junk, they say.
remark: A wizard in Al Kharid? She says I should expect the unexpected.
starter/compliment: Hello! Mia Persten, teleportation magic. Fancy a mystery?
starter/insult: You haven't heard of me? The creator of Home Teleport? Honestly!
starter/remark: Why do we hold our arms out to teleport? Nobody knows! Brilliant.

gossip: Nobody's seen that wizard by the gate in ages. Just gone.
compliment: Word is you found a temple under the sea. Under the sea!
You helped the wizards close some rift, they say. Good of you.
insult: Closed a rift into the Abyss, I hear. Right after it was opened.
trader/remark: Found a temple with a junk amulet? I'm in the wrong trade.

gossip: The old man by the limestone mine collects bones. For a museum.
remark: His sack talks, you know. The old man's sack. I've heard it.
starter/compliment: Errr... I'm an archaeologist. I need bones. Fresh ones.
starter/insult: Bones, boiled in vinegar. Can you manage that? Errr... can you?
starter/remark: Goblin, bear, frog, ram... errr, what was next? The sack knows.

compliment: You found all the old man's bones for him? Patient of you.
insult: Boiled bones in vinegar for a man with a talking sack. Sensible.
starter/compliment: Ah, my bone collector! Always on the lookout for fresh ones.
starter/insult: Errr... the museum thanks you. Sack, stop sniggering.
kid/remark: Did you really boil bones for the creepy old man? Yuck!

gossip: The old man wants more bones now. From Morytania to the desert.
starter/compliment: There are still a few bits and pieces I wouldn't mind, you know.
starter/insult: More bones, errr, for the displays. Unless you're squeamish?
starter/remark: Mumblemumble... yes, sack. I'm asking. More bones.

compliment: Every bone the old man wanted, they say. Every last one!
gossip: Heard the old man laughing up there. Went on for ages, it did.
insult: Finished his collection, I hear. Everyone will enjoy it, he says.
starter/compliment: My best collector! Everyone will enjoy my work. Everyone.
starter/insult: Sack says you missed a spot on that last bone. Sack's fussy.
kid/remark: The old man laughed for ages after you left. Is he poorly?

gossip: Gertrude's lost her cat Fluffs. Poor woman's beside herself.
Gertrude's boys saw the cat last. They're up to no good, those two.
kid/insult: Looking for a cat? Ask Wilough. Bring money. Lots.
starter/compliment: Have you seen my poor Fluffs? Please, could you look for her?
starter/insult: You'll look for Fluffs? You? Well, I suppose somebody must.
starter/remark: Fluffs, poor Fluffs. She never hurt anyone.

compliment: You brought Gertrude's cat home, they say. Kitten and all.
insult: Paid two children to find a cat, I hear. They saw you coming.
gossip: Gertrude's Fluffs had a kitten up at the old lumber yard. Fancy.
nan/compliment: Gertrude's cat's home safe. You're a good sort, dear.
kid/insult: Wilough says you paid him to find a cat. I can find cats too.
starter/compliment: Hello again! Fluffs is purring by my side, all thanks to you.
starter/insult: How's that kitten I gave you, dear? Fed, I hope. Brushed, I hope.

gossip: Sarah from the farm's put up a bounty. Some monster took her cart.
Something hulking came out of the trees by the crossroads, they say.
remark: Have you seen the notice board? There's a bounty on a monster.
rough/remark: Something's been at the crops up Falador way. Not foxes, either.

compliment: You're the one who saw off Sarah's monster? She's ever so pleased.
gossip: It was a sourhog, they say. Spits acid. Somebody made it!
A woman in a hood was asking after that bounty too, Sarah says.
insult: Fought a pig, I hear. A big one, mind. Spat at you, did it?
plain/insult: Got paid for a pig's foot, I hear. I'm in the wrong line of work.
kid/remark: Was it a giant pig? Did it spit at you? Did you keep the foot?

gossip: Kolodion changes shape when he duels, they say. Into what, though?
remark: Top wizards come from all over Gielinor to fight here, they say.
starter/compliment: I am the great Kolodion, master of battle magic. Care to duel?
starter/insult: Hah! A wizard of your level? Don't be absurd.
starter/remark: Many wizards fall in my arena, never to rise again.

compliment: You beat Kolodion in every shape? Even the demon? Blimey.
insult: Bested Kolodion, then went for a dip in a pool. Very mystical.
gossip: Another mage has chosen a god at the statues, they say.
starter/compliment: Ah, my battle mage. How are you? Enjoying the bloodshed?
starter/insult: You beat me once, traveller. Don't let it go to your head.

gossip: Kolodion says three strange powers are loose in the Wilderness.
They say a general of Zamorak walks the deep Wilderness now.
starter/compliment: Three beings, with power beyond even mine. Bring me their remains.
starter/insult: You have potential. But a wizard of your level? No chance.

compliment: You killed a Zamorakian general and a justiciar? Ye gods.
gossip: Servants of three gods fell in the Wilderness. One mage did it.
plain/insult: Killed champions of three gods for a better cape. Worth it?
shady/insult: You cut down Porazdir? Zamorak forgets nothing, meddler.
vicar/remark: A justiciar of Saradomin slain, they say. For a cloak. Dear me.
starter/compliment: Your cape carries the power of three gods now. Use it well.
starter/insult: Even my power has limits. Yours, I suspect, has many more.

gossip: That woman by the mountain says she's an archaeologist. Never digs.
There's an old door under the rocks by Ice Mountain, she reckons.
dwarf/remark: That human lass guards a pile of rocks all day. By Guthix, why?
starter/compliment: You there! Fancy some ancient ruins? Untold riches inside!
starter/insult: You'll do. I can't leave. Some other archaeologist might pinch it.
starter/remark: Untold riches in there. Er, history. Untold history.

compliment: You opened the old ruins under Ice Mountain? Found a dwarf, I hear!
gossip: That archaeologist was a grave robber all along! Ran off, she did.
insult: Fetched a sandwich for a thief, I hear. Very heroic.
plain/insult: Played rock paper scissors with a drunk dwarf, I hear. Who won?
dwarf/compliment: An Imcando dwarf, alive under the mountain! By Guthix!
kid/compliment: You learned to flex from a barbarian? Show me! Go on!

starter/compliment: Nilsal, traveller. Could you spare some cooked fish or meat?
starter/insult: No food? Never mind. I shall just sit here. Starving. Quietly.
starter/remark: I ran from the spiders. Further in. It seemed wise at the time.

starter/compliment: Nilsal, friend! Logosia will be thrilled with those tomes.
starter/insult: Thank you again for the food. Some salt next time, perhaps?
starter/remark: Ralos and Ranul, sun and moon. Our order began here, I'm sure.

gossip: The museum's found an island north of Morytania. Sending a barge!
Nine barges they've built for that island. Not one got there.
remark: One of the museum's barges sank because it didn't float. Imagine.
plain/insult: The museum wants someone brave for its cursed barge. Not you, then.
starter/compliment: You have the qualifications! Just the person for our voyage.
starter/insult: You have the qualifications, but I'm not sure you're ready.
starter/remark: An island north of Morytania. Easily the most interesting thing.

compliment: You got the museum's barge to that island! First one ever, they say.
gossip: The barge crew passed out on a sealegs potion! Someone else steered.
They say the seventh barge is still lost. Nobody's gone looking.
insult: Steered the barge while the crew lay out cold, I hear. Proper sailor.
guard/remark: The museum's sending folk to sea now. Not my department.
starter/compliment: Welcome to the museum! And thank you again for that voyage.
starter/insult: Ah, our navigator. The barge is still in one piece? Remarkable.

gossip: King Lathas wants that old outpost torn down. For an alchemists' lab.
remark: The fellow at the outpost keeps shouting 'All is lost!' at people.
starter/compliment: Wait a minute. You could help me! This building has history!
starter/insult: Don't bother, you're not experienced enough to help me!
starter/remark: All is lost! This great building will soon be in ruin.

compliment: You saved the old outpost, they say. It's a museum now.
gossip: The King's let the outpost be. A letter did it, they say.
insult: Got quizzed on a warrior's breakfast for a bit of history, I hear.
gnome/compliment: The outpost stands, human. Good. We like old things.
starter/compliment: Hurrah! My saviour! Do look round the new museum room.
starter/insult: Back again? Touch nothing. That's history, that is.

gossip: Sir Tiffy sits in the park all day. Recruiting, someone said.
Sir Tiffy's lot only take the clever ones, I hear. Brains first.
remark: That Sir Tiffy says 'what?' after everything. Everything, what?
sharp/insult: The Temple Knights want the clever sort. Ah. Well. Best of luck.
guard/gossip: Word from the castle: Sir Amik's sending another one to the park.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend! I may have put your name forward already. Erm.
starter/insult: Sir Tiffy tests for wits, friend. I did say you had some.
starter/remark: Sir Tiffy's in the park. I really ought to have told you more.

compliment: Passed Sir Tiffy's tests, they say. The clever sort, then.
An initiate of the Temple Knights? You kept that quiet.
insult: Word is the Temple Knights tested you with a fox and a chicken.
plain/insult: Sat Sir Tiffy's test without a stitch on, I hear. Bold.
gossip: Another initiate for Sir Tiffy, they say. Gold trim and all.
toff/compliment: One hears you've been made an initiate. Jolly good.
kid/insult: You did puzzles to be a knight? I'd have just hit someone.
starter/compliment: Hello, friend! Sir Tiffy tells me you did splendidly.
starter/insult: Ah, the initiate. Do try not to embarrass my letter.

gossip: Solus Dellagar's loose again, they say. The murder-mage himself.
Some clerk muddled an initiate's papers, I hear. Heads will roll.
remark: Lock your doors tonight. There's a mad mage on the loose.
sharp/insult: Sir Tiffy wants Solus caught. By someone competent, ideally.
guard/gossip: Word from the castle: watch for a mage. Wanted for murder.
starter/compliment: Ah, old bean! Bit of a muddle with your papers, what?
starter/insult: Five years a squire, dontchaknow. Unless there's a crisis, what?
starter/remark: Solus Dellagar loose again. Jolly bad show, what?

compliment: Word is you ran Solus Dellagar to ground. Well done.
A White Knight now, I hear. Sir Amik must be chuffed.
insult: Brought back a mage's hat as proof, I hear. Some trophy.
plain/insult: Had a bit of help catching that mage, I hear. A fair bit.
gossip: Solus Dellagar's been dealt with, they say. Sleep easy.
guard/compliment: A White Knight, are you? Then you know where the armoury is.
kid/compliment: You caught the murder-mage? Did he turn you into anything?
starter/compliment: Spiffing work with Solus, old bean! Absolutely first class.
starter/insult: Had a little help with Solus though, didn't you, what? Haw haw!

gossip: Witchaven folk are acting oddly, I hear. The mayor looks ill.
Witchaven's mayor is restoring some old shrine. Odd hobby.
remark: Nobody goes to Witchaven now. Not since that platform went up.
starter/compliment: Ah, old bean! Fancy a jaunt to Witchaven? Hush-hush, what?
starter/insult: Witchaven needs looking into. Do try not to get lost, what?
starter/remark: Odd business in Witchaven. Jolly odd, dontchaknow.

compliment: Word is you saved Witchaven from something nasty. Well done.
A giant slug under Witchaven, they say. Rather you than me.
insult: Slime on your boots again? Witchaven, was it?
plain/insult: Opened a sealed door for a sickly mayor, I hear. Clever.
gossip: They say there's something far worse than slugs off Witchaven.
kid/insult: You fought slugs? I squash those with my boot.
starter/compliment: Splendid show at Witchaven, old bean! Savant speaks highly.
starter/insult: Opened the door for the slugs, I hear. Bit of a gaffe, what?

gossip: The Sinclairs have upped and left the mansion. Just like that.
Nobody's seen King Arthur or his knights for ages. Odd, that.
Anna Sinclair's up for trial in Seers', they say. Her own father!
remark: Quiet at the mansion lately. Too quiet, if you ask me.
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! You didn't hear it from me, but the Sinclairs left!
starter/insult: Any interesting news? No? Then what are you standing around for?
starter/remark: The King gone, the Sinclairs gone. Quite a coincidence, I say.

compliment: Word is you brought King Arthur home. Camelot owes you.
You freed Merlin and the knights, they say. From Morgan Le Faye!
insult: Defended Anna Sinclair in court, I hear. Of all people.
gossip: Merlin's threatened to make rabbits of the Sinclairs, they say.
remark: The Sinclairs never leave the mansion now. Can't think why.
toff/remark: Arthur's back at the Round Table, one hears. Do keep up.
kid/compliment: You saved the King? Did Merlin really make frogs?
starter/compliment: Oh, it's you! Everyone's talking about Camelot. I said it first.
starter/insult: You might have told me first, you know. I'm the gossip here.

gossip: Trolls on Death Plateau again. They come down at night.
Harold lost the storeroom combination. He's been in the pub since.
remark: The Prince loves a puzzle, they say. The guards don't.
guard/gossip: Word from the camp: trolls raiding by night. Bar your door.
starter/compliment: Citizen! The trolls hold Death Plateau. Know another path?
starter/insult: You, citizen? My soldiers couldn't break through. Well, try.
starter/remark: A key would do. But no, the Prince is fond of puzzles.

compliment: Found a secret way up Death Plateau, they say. Good work.
Dunstan's boy is in the Imperial Guard now, thanks to you.
plain/insult: Beat a guard at dice for a scrap of paper, I hear. Heroic.
remark: Old Tenzing had a secret path all along. Who knew?
kid/compliment: You found the secret path! Show me! I won't tell the trolls.
starter/compliment: Welcome back, citizen! Burthorpe owes you.
starter/insult: A puzzle solved, citizen. Don't let it go to your head.

gossip: The raid went badly. Trolls took Dunstan's son, they say.
Godric's held in the Troll Stronghold. Poor Dunstan.
remark: Dunstan's beside himself. His boy's still with the trolls.
guard/gossip: Word from the camp: we were ambushed from the north. Stay sharp.
starter/compliment: Friend! The trolls took Godric. Will you go after him?
starter/insult: None of my men will go. I'd not blame you either, friend.
starter/remark: Ambushed from the north. We never stood a chance.

compliment: You brought Godric home from the trolls? Dunstan's overjoyed.
Beat a troll called Dad in his own arena, I hear. Blimey.
insult: Rescued Godric, and some mad old hermit too, I hear. Bonus.
gossip: Trolls are named after the first thing they try to eat, they say.
kid/remark: Trolls are named after what they eat first. What would you be?
starter/compliment: Welcome back, friend! Godric's safe, and that's your doing.
starter/insult: Back again, friend? The trolls haven't stopped raiding, mind.

gossip: Ug's crying again. Over Aga, they say. She's with Arrg.
Aga wants a Trollweiss flower. Nobody's seen one in years.
remark: Arrg's got other girlfriends, word is. Don't tell Aga.
starter/compliment: Man-thing! You help Ug? Maybe Ug not eat you!
starter/insult: Go away, man-thing, leave Ug alone!
starter/remark: Aga so beautiful. Smell like rotting dead ice wolf.

compliment: You beat Arrg, they say. Ug finally went to Aga.
plain/insult: Went sledging for a flower, I hear. For a troll. Romantic.
gossip: Arrg's lost all his swagger since a human beat him.
starter/compliment: Man-thing! You very strong and nice. Ug so happy!
starter/insult: You no touch Aga. Ug kill you. Ug just joke! Mostly.

gossip: Sanfew's after a herb only the trolls know. Goutweed, he says.
The druids are still purifying their stone circle. Slow work.
remark: Troll cooking needs a special herb, apparently. Trolls cook?
starter/compliment: Ah, young 'un! I need a herb the trolls call goutweed.
starter/insult: No doubt some other adventurer will come along who can help.
starter/remark: Goutweed... only the trolls know where it grows now.

compliment: Got goutweed out of the trolls for Sanfew, they say. Clever.
insult: Borrowed Tegid's dirty laundry, I hear. Rather you than me.
